places.notes: [Chinese · Kawaramachi, two-star creative Chinese behind a cell-like door] Through a barred, jail-like entrance off a Kawaramachi complex into a dark, sleek room with an open kitchen: owner-chef Yuji Iwasaki, ten years in hotel Chinese kitchens, opened in Ashiya in 2014 and moved here in 2019, and an October 2026 diner notes two Michelin stars since 2023. The chef's "add on" style layers flavours: foie gras monaka with hozuki jam, a gyoza rebuilt as chive custard under chive snow, char siu with fried bonito, almond tofu many call the best they've had. Portions are big. Lunch from ¥11,000 plus 10%; book on TableCheck. No vegetarian or gluten-free menus.

Chef Yuuzou Nakao cooks with a small team; diners call the chef young, unpretentious and easy to talk to. Book by phone for one of two seatings (17:00 or 19:30); a ¥4,000 charge covers the opening dishes, and most spend ¥20,000–30,000. Adults only.

Eat everything the same day, ideally on the Kamo riverbank a minute away. Some items can be reserved by phone to skip the queue. Cash only; closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

Portions are generous, so come as four or five and share. Getting in is the hard part: bookings open by phone at the end of each month for the next, and 2026 diners report hundreds of calls. places.notes: [Kissaten · Kawaramachi, the 1934 salon of free speech] Opened in 1934 down a lane off Shijo-Kobashi and designed by young artist friends of founder 立野正一, this European salon of stained glass, a white domed ceiling and red velvet chairs was meant as a place to talk about peace and art as wartime speech closed in; reviewers note it is a registered cultural property. Order the cake set — the house rare cheesecake with blueberry sauce, with coffee and fresh cream — or the special pudding. Open late, to 22:00, which suits a night after Minamiza. Cash only; no children; weekend queues.

An October 2026 review calls it a nationally registered tangible cultural property. places.notes: [Kaiseki · Oike, two hundred years of Kyoto ryori] Behind a white noren on Tomikoji-dori, a house that began in 1827 when the first master carried Wakasa fish along the 鯖街道 (the mackerel road) to the palace and court nobles. Sixth-generation 中村元計 (Motokazu Nakamura) — once a Zen trainee at 天龍寺 and now a doctor of food science — keeps the two dishes passed from father to son: sake-grilled guji, finished as a soup with hot water over the bones, and a white-miso zoni made without dashi. Courses are served in quiet private rooms over a courtyard; reviewers note three Michelin stars. Lunch around ¥20,000–30,000, dinner ¥40,000–50,000; book ahead; closed Sundays.
places.chef: Motokazu Nakamura (中村元計; official site, sixth-generation master, with the romaji Motokazu Nakamura) · Sixth-generation master (official site) · Per the official site: founded in Bunsei 10 (1827) when the first master, 若狭屋清兵衛, carried Wakasa fish such as guji and mackerel to Kyoto for the palace and court nobles; the second generation began catering; the third, a tea devotee, made tea kaiseki catering the core; the fourth supplied the inns 柊家, 俵屋 and 炭家 during the war; after the war the restaurant opened on its present site, and the fifth generation built today's base. The sixth, 中村元計, studied at Tokyo University of Fisheries, trained as a Zen monk at 天龍寺 in 嵯峨嵐山, and in 2021 earned a doctorate in food and agricultural science at 龍谷大学, approaching cooking as science. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2023; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. 2026 reviews call it Michelin three-starred. · 「即味心也」 — taste is the heart: only a person's heart moves another's (official site). · Sake-grilled guji; white-miso zoni.

The chef grows and picks some sixty kinds of vegetables each morning, and the light, consommé-seasoned courses are built around them — the signature terrine of separately cooked vegetables wrapped in cabbage, vegetable mousses, then fish or Omi beef. You leave light. Lunch from ¥9,800, dinner from ¥14,000, tax included and no service charge. Book by phone or Ikyu; no children 10 and under; closed Sundays.

Regulars praise the chef's stories and the couple's hospitality; one has been 35 times. About ¥20,000–30,000; book by phone; closed Mondays.

Small bags from ¥750 make light, long-keeping gifts. Takeaway only; come early; closed Wednesdays.

places.notes: [Kissaten · Karasuma Oike, the Corona egg sandwich] A retro coffee house in a building that was Kissa Seven for about 50 years from 1963; after its master died in 2011, the son looked for someone to keep the shop going, and Madrague opened that September. About a year later the free paper 音読 asked the shop to carry on the famous egg sandwich of Corona, a western-style restaurant that had just closed, and Corona's master came to teach it in person. The result is a fist-sized, hot, dashi-soft omelette on bread with demi-glace and mustard (¥1,180) — cut it in half to eat. Breakfast sets until 11:00; book a seat for 8:00, 9:30 or 12:00. Open daily 8:00–18:00 (irregular closures); cash only.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed on the official site), who opened the shop with the owner’s wife · Per the official site: before opening, the owner managed a café tied to the revival of Kyoto townhouses and old shopping streets and wanted to get back to hands-on work; while looking for a property with the owner’s wife, the couple met the son of the master of Kissa Seven (in business from 1963 for about 50 years; the master died in 2011) and opened Kissa Madrague there in September 2011. The name is that of Brigitte Bardot’s villa in Saint-Tropez; the owner’s wife loved the actress. The owner once worked part-time at Francois, near Corona, and often ate Corona’s egg sandwich on breaks. The site also describes a team, 京都喫茶文化遺産, formed to take over and keep old neighbourhood kissaten. Tabelog Kissaten "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2026. · Per the official site: to keep "the long-running neighbourhood kissaten with tradition", not a retro-styled café, and hand it on to the next generation. · Corona egg sandwich; Set A breakfast.

places.notes: [Tarte tatin café · Okazaki, half a century of tarte tatin] A small, old-fashioned café near Heian Shrine devoted to tarte tatin. Its story starts with the café 紅屋 that Yuri Matsunaga and husband 辰夫 opened in Gion in 1959; it became an art gallery, moved here in 1971 as a French restaurant beside the gallery, and turned into this café in 1987. Yuri kept baking the tarte tatin — honoured in France by the Confrérie des Lichonneux de tarte tatin in 2006 — until dying in 2014, and a grandchild bakes it now. About 20 apples go into each tart; pick from the day's varieties (Fuji ¥950 in 2026) and eat it warm with yogurt. No bookings; Tuesday–Sunday 11:30–18:00.
places.chef: Maya Wakabayashi · Granddaughter of the founder, named in a January 2016 article as carrying on the recipe; the official site says the recipe is now baked by the founder’s grandchild · Per the official site: the first owners, 松永ユリ (Yuri Matsunaga in Leaf Kyoto and Fashion Headline) and 辰夫, opened the café 紅屋, forerunner of LA VOITURE, in Gion in 1959; out of a love of art it became the gallery 紅 in 1964; in 1971 the business moved to Okazaki, where the French restaurant LA VOITURE opened alongside the gallery. Yuri, captivated by the tarte tatin served as a French dessert, kept baking it and was admitted in France to the Confrérie des Lichonneux de tarte tatin in 2006. The official site gives Yuri’s death in 2014 at 96; a January 2016 Fashion Headline article says Yuri died "two years ago at the age of 92", was born in the Taisho era, always sat in a corner of the shop, and created the recipe after eating tarte tatin on a trip to France. Leaf Kyoto (March 2021) adds that the daughter, Tomomi, helped open the 1971 restaurant and that the shop became a tarte tatin café in 1987. The omakase begins with a five-taste aperitif and the signature egg, then Kasumi crab with senmaizuke and caviar, Kyoto mushrooms, and Kyoto Hime beef cooked slowly for about 100 minutes. The tempura udon — big shrimp, a fluffy egg-thickened broth — and the dashi curry udon are what most reviewers order; any bowl can be had with soba instead. places.notes: [Izakaya · Shinkyogoku, a 1927 tavern with an abacus at the till] A real Showa-era taishu sakaba on the Shinkyogoku arcade, opened in 1927 by a founder who had come from Asakusa after the Great Kanto Earthquake, as a 'ten-sen shokudo' where everything cost ten sen. The marble counter and tables are the originals. Drink from noon at the counter or share a long table: Kirin draft, Gekkeikan sake, homemade croquettes (¥800), kizushi, oden, aji fry. A red slip goes to the register, where the bill is added on an abacus. Cash only; smoking allowed; at least one drink and one dish each. Closed Tuesday. One long-time customer found the food rushed and a server loud in October 2026, but keeps coming for the building and the atmosphere.

places.notes: [Wagashi · Nishiki Market, fu manju from an old nama-fu maker] The Nishiki Market counter of Fuka, a nama-fu maker that has supplied fresh wheat gluten to the Imperial Palace and to Kyoto ryotei since at least the 1860s. The thing to get is the fu manju its own history says Fuka created: smooth bean paste wrapped in chewy, aonori-green fu and a bamboo leaf (¥330–350), eaten chilled. Small fu taiyaki are baked to order (¥352). Two seats and a counter for eating on the spot, with Ippodo bancha for ¥100. 10:00–17:30, closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner, the 7th generation (official site; unnamed) · Per the official site: Fuka has long supplied fu to the Kyoto Imperial Palace; its founding year is unknown because its records burned in the upheavals of the late Edo period, but a pass for entering the palace is dated in the Keio era (1865–68), and the present owner is the 7th generation counted from then. Fuka helped bring nama-fu from plain temple cooking into Kyoto cuisine by delivering it fresh to ryotei every morning, and still works mainly to order for ryotei, making 30–40 kinds a day by hand from pumped groundwater with about 20 craftsmen, all of whom study the tea ceremony. The site says Fuka made the first nama-fu manju, an idea attributed to Emperor Meiji, who liked nama-fu. Tabelog Wagashi WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026. · Per the official site: the family business is "craft, not commerce" — use natural ingredients as far as possible and make by hand everything it can. · Fu manju; fu taiyaki.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: nama-fu is wheat gluten mixed with glutinous rice flour and steamed, and the fu manju and fu taiyaki are made from it (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: The fu manju is described as house-made smooth bean paste wrapped in nama-fu (wheat gluten and glutinous rice flour) flavoured with aonori and rolled in a bamboo leaf, with no animal ingredient named; a full ingredient list was not seen, so check (official site).

places.notes: [Wagashi · Gion, an old yokan shop down an alley] A small, Showa-feeling yokan shop hidden in an alley just off Shijo-dori in Gion, founded in 1884 according to reviewers. There is no one at the counter: ring the bell and the owner comes out (one reviewer describes a man in a white chef’s coat and black cap). The famous chestnut steamed yokan, packed with chunks of chestnut and wrapped in bamboo leaf (¥2,000), is seasonal — in September 2026 some visitors bought it and others were told it was not yet being made; there is also a silky mizu yokan, and small chilled steamed yokan (¥350) to eat on a walk. Flavours sell out by late afternoon — phone ahead for the big ones. Several reviewers call the service brusque. Cash only; closed Sunday.

places.cu: Spice-curry counter with one dish: keema curry (Serai, 2021), now in two kinds, beef and pork or chicken (2026 reviews) · stir-fried to order with a 17-spice mix (Serai, 2021); quite spicy, topped with fried and grilled eggplant, shishito, pumpkin and king oyster mushroom, a crunchy umeboshi in the middle, with homemade pickles · beef and pork keema with pickles: small (170 g rice) ¥1,350, medium…
places.notes: [Curry · Shijo Karasuma, one keema, very spicy] A 14-seat curry counter in the Muromachi back streets that serves a single dish: keema curry, beef and pork or chicken, stir-fried to order with a 17-spice mix, topped with grilled vegetables and an umeboshi, with homemade pickles and optional onion achaar. Expect real heat — staff warn that everything is spicy — and a 15–25 minute wait for your plate. Plates from about ¥1,350–1,700 in 2026, cash only. Queue from before 11:30; lunch Tuesday to Saturday, plus Tuesday dinner.
places.chef: 阿蘓慎太郎 · Owner (店主), per Serai (October 2021) · Yamagata Prefecture (Serai, 2021) · Per Serai (October 2021): the owner, 阿蘓慎太郎, is from Yamagata Prefecture and lived in Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto; before the shop, worked in promotion at a record company in Osaka, then took an early-retirement offer to become a curry cook and opened SPICE CHAMBER in 2010. The owner’s CDs, used for the shop’s music, line up beside the spice jars. The name translates as "spice room". The shop was in the 2021 Michelin Guide’s curry Bib Gourmand (Serai, 2021). Tabelog Curry WEST "Tabelog 100" 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024, 2026. · Keema curry (beef and pork, or chicken).
places.gfd: Ask. The keema is made from onions, tomatoes, minced meat and a 17-spice mix tempered in the pan (Serai, 2021) and served on rice with grilled vegetables, achaar and pickles; no gluten information is published.
places.vgd: Not vegan: the only food is keema curry of beef and pork or of chicken (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–15:00 Tuesday–Saturday; dinner 18:00–21:00 Tuesday only; closed Sunday and Monday (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog): a queue forms before opening (7th in line 10 min before opening on a September 2026 holiday; 5 ahead at 11:35 on an October 2026 weekday), with a 4-person bench outsid…

menu.en: Beef and pork keema curry with pickles, small / medium / la…

places.hood: First lane east, north of Shijo-Kawaramachi — 2 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Neighbourhood Edomae sushi at a U-shaped 17-seat counter, more than 50 years in business (Retty) · omakase nigiri: 8 pieces ¥2,000 (2021–22), ¥2,640 (January 2023); a sushi set for one ¥3,300 before tax (January 2025) · thick-sliced chu-toro sashimi, 8 slices ¥3,300 (February 2026) · extra pieces to order: chu-toro, squid, scallop, negi-toro, kanpachi, anago, toro-taku · the house negima soup (tu…
places.notes: [Sushi · Shijo-Kawaramachi, old-style counter] A family sushi counter up the first lane off Kawaramachi north of Shijo, in business for over 50 years: a U-shaped counter of 17 seats, large cuts on traditional rice, and the house negima soup of tuna and leek. A long-time regular found in January 2023 that the previous owner had handed over to a son. Omakase of 8 pieces was ¥2,640 in 2023; a set was ¥3,300 before tax in January 2025, and 8 thick slices of chu-toro sashimi ¥3,300 in February 2026. One dish per person; cash only. 17:00–22:00, closed Thursday; book by phone.
places.chef: Chef at the counter (unnamed); a son of the previous owner, per a January 2023 review · Retty describes a long-established sushi shop at Shijo-Kawaramachi with more than 50 years in business; a 2017 Retty review calls it a popular Edomae sushi shop of "50 years and more", and a 2015 Retty review says it was run by a friendly couple, another the warmth of a family business. A Tabelog review of a March 2021 visit describes a kind chef and the chef’s wife working quickly; a January 2023 diner, a regular under the previous owner, found the previous owner had passed the shop on to a son who looks just like the father. · Omakase nigiri; negima soup; toro-taku.
places.gfd: Ask. Nigiri omakase and sashimi plates; no gluten or soy-sauce information. Dislikes have been swapped out of the omakase when asked (November 2021).
places.vgd: Not vegan: every guest must order one dish, a fish sushi set or a sashimi plate (February 2026), and the house negima soup is tuna and leek.
places.hours: Tabelog: 17:00–22:00, closed Thursday; hours may change, check before visiting. Reservations taken by phone (075-221-6598); a January 2023 diner booked the same day and the counter filled at opening. One dish per person is required (a sashimi plate or a sushi set), drinks are optional (February 202…

places.n: ザ ノーザンライツコーナー (The Northern Lights Corner)
places.hood: Hanayu Koji alley off Shinkyogoku, north of Shijo — 1 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Afternoon-to-late standing bar with a terrace, from the company behind Gion’s Finlandia Bar (official site; Tabelog) · no cover charge; recommended drinks in the low ¥1,000s (2025 reviews) · Earl Grey gin and tonic ¥1,300, yuzu gin and tonic ¥1,300 (October 2025); seasonal fruit Bellinis (Shine Muscat, Asian pear) and a strawberry rum cocktail; Moscow mule, China Blue, Grasshopper, Naked and Famo…
places.notes: [Bar · Shinkyogoku, a drink from 3 pm] A standing bar with a small terrace at the mouth of the Hanayu Koji alley off Shinkyogoku, opened in 2013 by K-stage, the company that runs Gion's Finlandia Bar; it was named for the aurora, as a curtain of light over the alley. No cover charge and most drinks in the low ¥1,000s: gin and tonics with Earl Grey or yuzu (¥1,300), seasonal fruit Bellinis, a long whisky list. A year-end regular praises the young manager's knowledge; smoking is allowed inside, so non-smokers take the terrace. 15:00–23:00.
places.chef: Bar of K-stage (株式会社ケイ・ステージ), which also runs ぎをん FINLANDIA BAR, The Common One Bar Kyoto, Turquoise Bar and ぎをん新橋 何生庵 · Per the K-stage company history: in August 2013 the company opened The Northern Lights Corner on the ground floor and the more formal Bar The Northern Lights on the first floor of the new Hare no Hi Hanayu Koji building in Shinkyogoku (the upstairs bar closed in December 2021; the space is now an office of アルコ・ノルディック株式会社, the company’s vodka importer). The name wishes for a curtain of light like the aurora over Hanayu Koji. The corner bar first opened at 14:00 and now opens at 15:00. K-stage took over Gion’s Finlandia Bar (founded February 1982 as a sister to the Finnish restaurant FINLANDIA, opened at Gojo-Yanaginobaba in 1976) in November 2002. Tabelog’s note calls it Finlandia’s first try at a standing bar. A June 2025 review says staff sometimes rotate between the sister bars. · Per the official site: opened as a bar for a light drink from midday, with everything from beer to proper cocktails to enjoy casually. · Gin and tonics; seasonal fruit cocktails; whisky.
places.gfd: Ask. A drinks bar: beer, gin and tonics, whisky and cocktails; the only food reviewers mention is potato bread and cream cheese with rum raisins on crackers (March 2025).
places.vgd: Ask. Spirits and fruit cocktails may suit; some cocktails use cream (a Grasshopper, June 2025) and the snacks seen include cream cheese.
places.hours: Official site: 15:00–23:00 (last order 22:30), opened as a bar for a light drink from the afternoon; Tabelog also gives 15:00–23:00 every day; an October 2025 review gave 15:00–24:00 with irregular closures. No cover charge (Tabelog; 2025 reviews). Bookings taken (Tabelog). Mostly standing at the c…

places.n: イル ギオットーネ 京都本店 (IL GHIOTTONE Kyoto honten)
places.hood: Below the Yasaka Pagoda, Higashiyama — 8 min walk from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: "What if Italy had a region called Kyoto?" — Italian courses built on Kyoto ingredients (official site) · lunch Pranzo A ¥6,000 (3 antipasti, 1 pasta, main, dessert and coffee), B ¥8,000 (2 pasta), C ¥12,000 and D ¥16,000; dinner Cena A ¥12,000, B ¥16,000, C ¥20,000; tax and service extra (official site) · 2026 dishes: charcoal-grilled sea snail and tairagi, burrata with autumn fruit, caviar and …
places.notes: [Italian · Yasaka Pagoda, Kyoto as an Italian region] Chef-owner Yasuhiro Sasajima's restaurant in a converted townhouse right beside the Yasaka Pagoda, open since 2002 and built on one idea: what if Italy had a region called Kyoto? Courses only, lunch from ¥6,000 and dinner from ¥12,000 (plus tax and service): Kyoto vegetables and seasonal fish, two pastas with cheese or truffle grated at the table, charcoal-grilled meat. Italian WEST Tabelog 100 (2021, 2023, 2025). One September 2026 diner found the floor short-staffed. Lunch and dinner, closed Tuesday and Wednesday; book online.
places.chef: Yasuhiro Sasajima (笹島保弘) · Owner-chef (オーナーシェフ, official site) · Osaka Prefecture (Serai, 2013) · Born in Osaka Prefecture in 1964 (Serai, from its spring 2013 issue). Bunshun Online (2017) recalls the chef at イル・パッパラルド in Kyoto, with generous, energetic, reasonably priced plates, and dates the chef’s independence to 2002, launching IL GHIOTTONE as "Italian sent out from Kyoto": courses based on kombu dashi, scented with kinome and yuzu, with Kyoto vegetables such as Kujo leek and Shogoin turnip. Serai gives the Kyoto opening as 2002 and a Marunouchi (Tokyo) branch as 2005; the official site now lists the Kyoto honten, the wine shop Officina IL GHIOTTONE KYOTO (which also sells the group’s frozen pasta sauces) and IL GHIOTTONE DI PIÙ in Grand Front Osaka. Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023 and 2025. A September 2026 diner praised the service of the chef’s wife. · Per the official site: the cooking grew from the thought "what if Italy had a region called Kyoto?" — the chef’s answer, as a Japanese cook, to the meaning of going on making the Italian food the chef loves in Japan: Italian cooking found only in Japan. · Kyoto-ingredient Italian courses; chitarra and tagliatel…
places.gfd: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Every course has two pasta courses (chitarra, orecchiette, tagliatelle, linguine) plus house focaccia and bread (2026 reviews; official course list); a September 2026 diner who pre-ordered had disliked ingredients left out, so some changes are made.
places.vgd: Ask when booking. No vegetarian course is listed; courses run on fish, shellfish, duck, lamb, veal and beef, with burrata and Parmigiano (2026 reviews). A September 2026 diner noted many vegetable dishes.
places.hours: Tabelog: lunch 12:00–14:00 and dinner 18:00–20:00 (both times are the last seating), closed Tuesday and Wednesday; changes to closing days on the official website. Booking online (Toreta, via the official site) or by phone; a September 2026 diner booked a weekday lunch about a month ahead, and the …

places.n: たかつじ 佳粋 (Takatsuji Kasui)
places.hood: Takatsuji-dori, Shimogyo-ku — 5 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Counter izakaya with Japanese and some Western dishes and a deep sake list (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · first-visit set of appetiser, soup and sashimi ¥3,000 (September and October 2026): in autumn simmered grilled eggplant, a jelly and sesame tofu, a shrimp-dumpling soup with winter melon and sudachi, bonito and kombu-cured sea bream · à la carte without printed prices: vinegared sardine, whelk and…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Takatsuji-dori, a hidden counter] A 14-seat counter izakaya behind a heavy iron door at the back of a building on Takatsuji-dori, opened in March 2023 by the former owner of Kasui in Pontocho. A first visit starts with appetisers, a dashi soup and sashimi (¥3,000 in 2026), then à la carte — vinegared fish, nuta, grilled Spanish mackerel — and donabe rice, the leftovers sent home as onigiri in a paper bag with a drawing of the owner. Prices are not printed; ask. Izakaya WEST Tabelog 100 2025 and 2026. Overseas guests book through their hotel front desk or in person. Evenings, from 16:00 at weekends.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed), the former owner of Kasui in Pontocho · A Tabelog review of a March 2023 visit says the owner of the former Pontocho shop Kasui reopened in Takatsuji after three years; a March 2023 Retty review likewise says the owner ran 佳粋 in Pontocho before opening Takatsuji Kasui. Tabelog gives the opening day as 28 March 2023. A September 2026 diner found two staff running the counter with jazz playing; another remembered the master in a bow tie. Tabelog izakaya WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025 and 2026; Tabelog Hot Restaurant 2026. · Dashi soups; donabe rice; sake.
places.gfd: Ask when booking: the shop asks guests to state allergies when reserving and will do its best, but may not always be able to accommodate (Tabelog). No gluten information; dishes include nuta with miso, dashi soups and seasoned rice.
places.vgd: Not vegan: every first visit is served a soup and two small dishes (Tabelog), and the soup is a dashi broth, in 2026 with shrimp dumpling; the rest of the menu is fish, shellfish and sashimi.
places.hours: Tabelog: Monday–Friday 17:00–23:00, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 16:00–23:00, last order 22:00; closed irregularly. Bookings taken; the shop does not accept bookings from overseas guests because of no-shows — visitors should book through their hotel front desk or come in person beforehand, and boo…

places.n: 御二九と八さい はちべー (Oniku to Yasai Hachibe)
places.hood: Yanagi-koji alley off Shinkyogoku, north of Shijo — 3 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: "Niku kappo" of beef offal (uchiniku), with Kyoto vegetables and seasonal ingredients, using Japanese, Western and Chinese techniques (official site; Tabelog) · evening omakase, about 12–13 dishes, ¥8,800: liver-pâté salad, beef-tongue dumpling stew, tail, blanched mino and senmai tripe, fried trachea cartilage (urute), aorta in Chinese dressing, Achilles tendon with ponzu, grilled cuts cooked by…
places.notes: [Beef-offal kappo · Yanagi-koji off Shijo] A small two-storey house on the stone-paved Yanagi-koji alley, named after the nearby Hachibei Myojin shrine, serving beef offal as Kyoto-style kappo. Evenings are one omakase of about a dozen dishes (¥8,800) — Achilles tendon with ponzu, aorta, liver with garlic chives, tripe — with the grilling done for you at the counter and a beef-tongue harihari hot pot finished with Chinese noodles. Lunch is a harami rice bowl with vegetables (¥2,500), no booking. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed in the sources); run by the yagenbori group · Per the yagenbori group site: one of the group’s six Kyoto restaurants (with 花見小路やげんぼり, 出逢ひ茶屋おせん, しぐれ茶屋侘助, 祇をん う桶や う and 花遊小路 江戸川); each cut is prepared one by one so that the texture, flavour and nourishment of beef offal come through. Per Tabelog (operator text): the name comes from the Hachibei Myojin shrine nearby. A March 2026 reviewer had eaten the harami bowl at lunch several times before the pandemic. · Per the official site: to overturn the idea of horumon by drawing out its flavour to the limit with careful handwork. · Beef-tongue harihari hot pot with Chinese noodles; harami rice bowl.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free in practice: the evening course runs through soy-marinated and ponzu-dressed offal, fried cartilage and a Chinese-noodle finish in the hot-pot broth; lunch comes with red miso soup and a soy-marinated heart dish (official menu; 2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a beef-offal restaurant — every course dish and lunch plate is built on beef (official menu).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–14:30, dinner 17:00–23:00; closed Tuesday (official site). Tabelog gives last entry at 14:00 for lunch (until sold out) and 21:30 for dinner. Lunch cannot be booked — come to the shop; the evening is a single omakase course, best booked (official site; Tabelog). Corkage ¥3,000 a bottle,…

places.n: 酒呑にし川 柳小路店 (Shuten Nishikawa Yanagikoji)
places.hood: Yanagi-koji alley north of Shijo — 2 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Sake izakaya with about 30–40 local sakes from all over Japan and daily obanzai of Kyoto vegetables (Tabelog) · three-sake tasting ¥1,000, also a limited-edition tasting and free-flow (2026 reviews) · sashimi platter (small size is generous), firefly squid in soy sauce, cucumber with meat miso, salted squid with cream cheese ¥890, sea bream with Kujo green onion ¥1,090, sesame mackerel ¥1,080, cl…
places.notes: [Sake izakaya · Yanagi-koji off Shijo] A ten-seat sake bar in a row house on Yanagi-koji, where guests share one big slab table split by a low partition. The draw is the sake: around 30–40 local brews, poured as three-glass tastings (¥1,000) or free-flow, with generous plates of sashimi, obanzai and snacks (¥790–1,390). Open from 15:00 daily (earlier on some days, per reviewers) to 23:00; book ahead. Its sister shop is at Kawaramachi Gojo.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed in the sources) · Opened 29 November 2020 (Tabelog). The same name has a shop at Kawaramachi Gojo (Tabelog 26036839, opened 14 January 2022); an April 2026 reviewer had been to a Kyoto Station branch that has since closed. A July 2026 review says the local sakes come from Koyama Shoten. · Per Tabelog (operator text): a casual place for seasonal obanzai and carefully chosen sake, welcoming solo diners. · Three-sake tastings; obanzai; sashimi platter.
places.gfd: Ask. Sashimi, grilled fish, tofu and obanzai, but many dishes use soy sauce, dashi or miso (firefly squid in soy sauce, cucumber with meat miso, grilled vegetables in dashi); no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan in practice: the food is sashimi, fish, shellfish, meat miso and dashi-based obanzai (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 15:00–23:00 every day, closing days not fixed (generally open year-round); hours may change, so booking is advised (Tabelog). Reviewers also drank here at lunch: a March 2026 review gives opening at 13:00, and an April 2026 visitor was the only lunch guest. 10 counter seats; parties of up to 4; pri…

places.hood: South of the Imperial Palace, near Karasuma-Marutamachi — 4 min from Marutamachi Stn
places.cu: Bistro of meat, game and charcoal grilling with spices and sauces, plus Japanese ingredients (2025–26 reviews) · homemade Yonezawa-pork ham and rillettes, pâté, spiced lamb stew, charcoal-roasted Ezo venison, magret and Moulard duck, raw-beef hamburg steak, lamb steak · fish: Donchicchi horse mackerel with passion fruit, fried young sweetfish (one in semolina), Moroccan-style charcoal-grilled oct…
places.notes: [Meat bistro · south of the Imperial Palace, game over charcoal] A stylish 20-seat bistro near Marutamachi with a counter facing the kitchen, known for meat: house ham, rillettes and pâté, spiced lamb, charcoal-roasted Ezo venison and duck — but the kitchen also turns Japanese fish into spiced, sauced plates, like octopus with couscous or sweetfish fritters, and ends with a mango curry. The menu carries no prices; expect about ¥10,000–15,000 a head with wine. Book ahead. Dinner from 18:00 (weekend lunch reported); closed Thursday and the third Wednesday.
places.chef: Chef (unnamed in the sources) · Opened 27 March 2017 (Tabelog). Tabelog Steak/Teppanyaki WEST "Tabelog 100" 2024. A November 2025 reviewer says the shop used to serve a regular lunch of curry and burgers before bringing back a weekend lunch course. · Charcoal-grilled game and duck; homemade ham; mango curry.
places.gfd: Ask. Charcoal-grilled meats and fish are the core, but there are fritters, spring rolls, quiche, semolina-coated sweetfish, curry and bread; no gluten information (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan in practice: a meat-and-game bistro (ham, rillettes, venison, duck, lamb), with fish dishes and cream; a few vegetable plates such as the zucchini steak come with a shellfish paste (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–22:00; closed Thursday and the third Wednesday; hours may change (Tabelog). A November 2025 reviewer reported a weekend-only lunch course (appetizers, bread, choice of main) restarting, and a February 2026 reviewer had it; Tabelog lists dinner only. Booking is essential (July 2026). The menu …

places.hood: Shijo-dori between Karasuma and Kawaramachi, basement — 5 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Coffee specialist in a dim, retro basement, with the coffees likened to actors on the menu (2026 reviews) · Red blend, the shop’s most popular (100 g beans ¥850 online), White blend, Geisha, Yemen Golden Mocha, Kopi Luwak, 8-hour cold brew (official shop; 2026 reviews) · hot Vienna coffee, coffee float ¥980, coffee soft serve ¥700, fresh coffee jelly ¥800, rich cheesecake, fondant au chocolat (20…
places.notes: [Kissaten · Shijo-dori, a coffee house underground] Down a staircase off Shijo-dori, a dim, retro basement café with sofas, solo counter seats with outlets and a walled-off smoking room. The house Red blend is the easy choice; there are also single origins up to Geisha and Kopi Luwak, an 8-hour cold brew, and a coffee float (¥980), fresh coffee jelly (¥800) and a molten fondant au chocolat. Orders by smartphone at the table. 10:00–19:00 (Monday from 11:00); weekday seats can be booked.
places.chef: Run by 株式会社生きている珈琲; the online shop names 小林弘樹 as the person responsible for sales · Opened 15 January 2011 (Tabelog). Tabelog Kissaten "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2026. Per a November 2026 review: each cup is brewed from 25 g of coarsely ground beans in a cone-shaped flower dripper, and the beans are roasted in a hot-air, low-temperature roaster said to bring out sweetness without damaging the beans. The official site sells beans by mail order. · Per the official site: care over the space where the coffee is served, with areas for families, couples and business meetings, and full separation of smoking seats. · Red blend; 8-hour cold brew; fresh coffee jelly.
places.gfd: Ask. Coffee is the focus; the food is cheesecake, fondant au chocolat, coffee jelly and soft serve, with no ingredient list published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Black coffee and cold brew suit; the desserts, Vienna coffee, floats and soft serve use cream, milk or eggs (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tuesday–Sunday and public holidays 10:00–19:00, Monday 11:00–19:00 (last order 18:20); closed 31 December and 1 January; occasional changes (official site; Tabelog). Bookings on weekdays only (Tabelog). Ordering is by mobile order at the table (October 2026). Smoking is allowed only in a walled-off…

places.n: 炭焼 やないの (Sumiyaki Yanaino)
places.hood: Ura-Teramachi just north of Shijo — 3 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Charcoal-grill izakaya of fish and pork skewers rather than chicken (a January 2026 diner notes that no yakitori is served) · skewers from one piece: kombu-cured mackerel ¥420, seasonal pork rolls ¥350, shishamo ¥280, salmon belly ¥300, kuruma prawn ¥420, oyster with sudachi ponzu ¥420, spicy cod roe ¥330, Kyotanba highland pork steak ¥350 · sashimi such as flounder ¥1,400, amberjack ¥1,300, yoko…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Ura-Teramachi, charcoal skewers of fish and pork] A small charcoal-grill izakaya down Ura-Teramachi, with eight counter seats in front of the grill and a tatami room upstairs. The skewers are fish and pork, not chicken: kombu-cured mackerel, oysters with sudachi ponzu, kuruma prawn, and pork rolled round seasonal vegetables — Kujo green onion, shiso, lettuce. The smoked-mackerel macaroni salad is the house's must-order, and the sashimi comes with generous wasabi and ginger. Skewers from ¥280; a May 2026 table found the value excellent, a June 2026 pair paid ¥13,000 for a light meal. Smoking is allowed. Closed Thursday.
places.chef: 木村 高行 · Owner (the invoice holder) · The invoice register lists an individual, 木村 高行, as the holder of the shop’s invoice number (registered 1 October 2023). Opened 12 November 2020 (Tabelog). Staff explain the dishes in detail (December 2025). · Pork-roll skewers; kombu-cured mackerel skewer; smoked-mackerel macaroni salad.
places.gfd: Ask. Skewers are mostly salted, but the menu also has ponzu, soy-marinated and fried dishes (chikuwa tempura, kara-age) and oyster soy sauce; no gluten information is published (Tabelog menu, May 2026).
places.vgd: Ask. Fish and pork skewers make up most of the menu; vegetable skewers (lotus root, ginkgo, broad beans, zucchini) appear in 2025–26 reviews, but their seasoning is not stated.
places.hours: 16:00–22:30 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday; 15:00–22:00 Sunday; closed Thursday and on some other days (Tabelog). Bookings taken; parties over two hours by arrangement; the 2nd-floor tatami room seats 5–8 and can be booked (Tabelog). 16 seats (8 at the counter, 8 on tatami); smokin…

places.n: だいあん 河原町木屋町店 (Diane Kawaramachi Kiyamachi)
places.hood: Kiyamachi by the Takase River — 3 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Large Kiyamachi izakaya of sushi, tempura and Kyoto dishes, known on social media for all-you-can-eat shrimp shabu-shabu (2026 reviews) · shrimp shabu-shabu: 8–10 head-on shrimp each to start, eaten raw or swished in a broth that deepens with the shrimp heads, finished with ramen; ¥5,980 (May 2026), ¥4,980 (September 2025) · dashimaki topped with ikura ¥968 · Sushi Dogs (sea urchin and green onio…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Kiyamachi, all-you-can-eat shrimp shabu-shabu] A two-floor izakaya on Kiyamachi with windows over the Takase River, popular for its all-you-can-eat shrimp shabu-shabu (¥5,980 in May 2026): big head-on shrimp to eat raw or swish in a broth that grows richer with every head, then ramen in the broth to finish. Ordering stops after 60 minutes, and reviewers say no one warns you, so order early. Reviewers praise the shrimp; some found the side dishes average and, in May–June 2026, the floor sticky. The menu also runs to Kyoto dishes — yudofu, yuba, nama-fu dengaku — and Sushi Dogs. Daily 17:00–23:00.
places.chef: Run by 株式会社ＣＲＯＷＮ (Sakai, Osaka; invoice T9120001167719); no person is named · The invoice number on Tabelog (T9120001167719) belongs to 株式会社ＣＲＯＷＮ, head office in Sakai, Osaka (NTA corporate-number site). places.cu: Magic-themed mixology bar: "Stage Magic" cocktails grouped by the show that comes with them — ALCHEMY, FIRE, SMOKE, BANG — e.g. Fudo Myo-o, Death in Provence, Strawberry Ichie and Get Your Spirit Back (¥2,500 each in December 2025), smoky old fashioned; also standard cocktails and omakase cocktails (2024–26 reviews)
places.notes: [Cocktail bar · Shijo-Kiyamachi, magic in a glass] A small second-floor bar like a wizard's den — swing chairs, a restroom behind a bookshelf, loud music on the stairs — where each "Stage Magic" cocktail comes with its own trick, chosen by style: alchemy, fire, smoke or bang. Most staff and guests are from overseas and English is the working language. Cocktails about ¥2,000–2,500 with service included. No bookings and it fills fast, so come at opening. Smoking allowed. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Christoph · Owner, a professional magician (per a January 2024 review) · Opened 14 February 2015 (Tabelog). Per 2024–26 reviews: a magic bar where the bartenders perform with the drinks, with guest participation; in March 2024 about 90% of guests were from overseas and most staff did not speak much Japanese, while a November 2025 reviewer found the Japanese staff fluent in English. · Stage Magic cocktails.
places.gfd: Ask. A cocktail bar; the drinks use spirits, liqueurs and syrups whose ingredients are not published, and a reviewer mentions food without naming it (2024–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Cocktails only are described; ingredients such as egg white, cream or honey are not listed (2024–26 reviews).
places.hours: 19:00–1:00, Tuesday to Sunday; closed Monday; hours may change (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2024 found it opening at 20:00 and nearly full at once, with a queue before opening. No reservations (Tabelog; November 2025): late arrivals stand at the side counter. 12 seats plus standing; smoking allowed (Tab…

places.hood: Nijo-dori just east of Kiyamachi, near The Ritz-Carlton — 5 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae…
places.cu: Cocktail and whisky bar: a long shelf of whisky, cocktails made to the guest’s taste, the house gin and tonic (2026 reviews) · cocktails such as a Quarter Deck with wasanbon sugar and a Stinger; Calvados, rum, sherry brandy; bourbon with soda; cigars (2026 reviews) · gin and tonic ¥1,100, vanilla ice cream ¥900 (July 2026) · food: chicken liver pâté, kinmedai carpaccio, oil sardines, house-smoked…
places.notes: [Bar · Kiyamachi-Nijo, a Kyoto bar institution since 1994] A big, bright second-floor bar on Nijo-dori near the Kamo River, often named first when Kyoto drinkers are asked for a bar: a semicircular counter where several bartenders work, a casual floor for groups, a deep whisky shelf and cigars. The gin and tonic is the house signature — reviewers say new bartenders must master it — and the cocktails are built around the sweetness of the spirit. Counter charge ¥550; gin and tonic ¥1,100. 18:00–2:00, closed Monday and Tuesday.
places.chef: Bar team; a June 2026 review names the chief bartender as Sawada · Opened 24 March 1994 (Tabelog). Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022. The official site also runs 角打酒場KASK (open every day 14:00–2:00) and Cave de K (15:00–0:00, closed Tuesday). Per a July 2026 review: many well-known Kyoto bartenders trained here, and making a gin and tonic to K6’s standard is a required test for bartenders joining. · Per a June 2026 review: K6’s cocktails are designed to bring out the hidden sweetness of the spirits. · Gin and tonic; whisky; cigars.
places.gfd: Ask. A bar with a food menu of pâté, carpaccio, oil sardines, house-smoked quail eggs and cheese, pizza, pasta and fries; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Spirits and many cocktails suit; the food is mostly meat, fish and cheese (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–2:00; closed Monday and Tuesday (official site; Tabelog); last food order 1:00 (July 2026). Bookings by phone (Tabelog; June 2026). A ¥550 charge applies at the bar counter, not on the casual floor (July 2026). 40 seats: a large semicircular counter and group seating; smoking allowed, and cig…

places.n: セクションドール (Section D'or)
places.hood: Okazaki, west of Heian Shrine — 4 min from the Higashiyama-Nijo bus stop
places.cu: One dish only: a tandoori-chicken plate, ¥2,700, with a generous spread of seasonal grilled vegetables (pumpkin, butternut squash, eggplant, okra, lotus root, yam, turnip, tsurumurasaki and more) and bread for the juices; mild rather than hot, closer to a light Italian plate than a typical Indian one (2026 reviews) · drinks: oolong teas, cold-brewed and frozen, Taiwanese Dong Ding; wine (2026 rev…
places.notes: [Tandoori chicken · Okazaki, one plate done well] A quiet eight-seat room in an Okazaki apartment building that serves a single dish: tandoori chicken, crisp-skinned and juicy, mildly spiced, on a plate crowded with seasonal grilled vegetables that regulars come back for each season (¥2,700). Order an oolong tea with it. Book ahead, even same day. Cash only; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed in the sources) · Opened 1 April 2011 (Tabelog). Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026. · Tandoori-chicken plate with seasonal vegetables.
places.gfd: Ask. The only dish is tandoori chicken with grilled vegetables, served with bread; the marinade ingredients are not published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the single menu item is a tandoori-chicken plate (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–14:00, dinner 17:30–21:00; closed Tuesday; hours may change (Tabelog). Bookings taken, even on the day (October 2026); the owner said few come on rainy days without a booking (June 2026). 8 seats at 4 tables (Tabelog; an October 2026 reviewer counted four seats); non-smoking; cash only …

places.n: カジュアル割烹 とのみず (Casual Kappo Tonomizu)
places.hood: South of Shijo, west of Kawaramachi, basement — 4 min walk from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: À la carte kappo, "Japanese cuisine and kappo in a new way" (Tabelog), with over 20 sakes chosen by season (Tabelog) · opener of soup and three small dishes ¥1,650 (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · assorted sashimi, botan shrimp marinated in junmai sake, foie gras miso-cured and wrapped in kombu-cured sea bream (the dish "everyone posts about"), wagyu cheek simmered Koshu-style with crumbled sesame tofu,…
places.notes: [Kappo · Kawaramachi, kappo cooking by the dish] A 12-seat basement counter near Kawaramachi where one cook turns out kappo food à la carte, so you order what you like instead of a set course. Dinner opens with a booked soup-and-small-dishes starter (¥1,650); then come sashimi, the much-photographed foie gras wrapped in kombu-cured sea bream, wagyu cheek with sesame-tofu sauce, oden in the cold months and a clay-pot rice of matsutake with eel or saury, with the 'staff meal' pasta that reviewers rave about to finish. Over 20 seasonal sakes. Bills ran ¥6,000–15,000 a head in 2026. Charcoal smoke can drift over the counter. Open daily 17:00–23:00.
places.chef: Owner-chef, who cooks alone (unnamed in the sources) · Per an August 2026 review: the owner is 40, trained at a ryokan in Fukui and a kaiseki restaurant in Pontocho, and cooks everything alone, with a female staff member serving; an October 2026 diner was surprised at the speed with one person cooking. A September 2026 regular asks "the manager" to choose the sake. · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): "Dishes to Enjoy Japanese Cuisine and Kappo in a New Way"; young customers and sake lovers welcome; suited to solo diners, dates and groups of 2–4. · Foie gras with kombu-cured sea bream; clay-pot rice; staff-meal pasta.
places.gfd: Ask. Dashi-based kappo cooking with soy-based seasonings, tempura, kara-age, oden with fish cakes and a pasta to finish; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the cooking rests on dashi, fish, eel, duck and wagyu (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30) every day; closing days may vary (Tabelog). Reservations online or by phone; dinner starts with a booked "one soup" opener of soup and small dishes, ¥1,650, then à la carte (Tabelog; August 2026); an extra appetizer is +¥550 (August 2026). Full by 18:00 on a September…

places.n: 京鴨とsake 鴨蔵 (Kyogamo to Sake Kamokura)
places.hood: Kiyamachi-dori south of Shijo, between the Kamo and Takase rivers — 2 min from Kyoto Kawa…
places.cu: Izakaya built on 京鴨 (Kyoto duck), Kyoto vegetables and rice, with Fushimi sake and Tanba wine (Tabelog) · low-temperature duck breast sushi with sea urchin, Kyoto-duck sukiyaki, duck shabu-shabu finished with soba (Tabelog; October 2026) · five-skewer duck platter (negima, roast, liver, heart, bonjiri), grilled duck neck, dashimaki of Kyoto-duck eggs, simmered duck roast and confit, Kyoto-vegetab…
places.notes: [Duck izakaya · Kiyamachi, Kyoto duck from sushi to sukiyaki] A duck-only izakaya on Kiyamachi, between the Kamo and Takase rivers, with a counter, tables and sunken kotatsu rooms in reclaimed wood. Kyoto duck turns up as skewers (liver, heart, bonjiri), a slow-cooked roast, sushi with sea urchin, dashimaki from duck eggs, and in two hot pots — sukiyaki or shabu-shabu finished with soba. Lunch is duck seiro soba with tempura. Courses with free-flow drinks run ¥6,500–10,500; evenings carry an ¥800 starter charge. Popular dishes sell out early, so book or come early. Lunch and dinner daily.
places.chef: Company-run restaurant (a corporate invoice registrant, Tabelog); no staff named · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): creative dishes from fresh Kyoto ingredients, especially the brand duck 京鴨, Kyoto rice and vegetables; local drinks such as Fushimi sake and Tanba wine, including rare once-a-year brands; a calm room in reclaimed wood with sunken-kotatsu private rooms. · Kyoto-duck sukiyaki; duck skewers; duck seiro soba.
places.gfd: Ask. Duck seiro with soba, tempura, duck katsu, pizza and sukiyaki with a soy-based sauce are on the menu; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and Kyoto-vegetable tempura and grilled vegetables are served, but nearly everything centres on duck, the hot pots use duck broth and the soba dip is duck-based (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:30) daily; dinner Monday–Friday 17:00–22:00, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 16:00–22:00 (last orders food 21:30, drinks 21:45) (Tabelog). Evening cover charge (otoshi) ¥800; a service charge is added on 1–3 January (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; walk-ins possible …

places.n: 松之助 京都本店 (Matsunosuke Kyoto honten)
places.hood: Takakura-dori south of Oike — 3 min walk from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cu: Café and pantry of New England–style American baking (official site; 2026 review) · apple pies, takeaway (eat-in) prices: sour cream apple pie all year ¥770 (¥784), Big Apple Pie October–March ¥890 (¥1,111), custard ¥770 (¥958), maple ¥820 (¥988) and caramel ¥810 (¥968) apple pies in autumn–winter, 14 Lincoln Street apple pie in spring ¥770 (¥784) · cherry pie ¥780, banana cream pie ¥760, chocola…
places.notes: [American bake shop · Takakura Oike, apple pie since 2000] The café and pantry that the Kyoto cookery researcher 平野顕子 opened in 2000 after studying New England baking in Connecticut. The glass-fronted white room serves American pies and cakes from a showcase — the sour cream apple pie all year, the Big Apple Pie from October, custard, maple and caramel apple pies through winter — plus cheesecakes, scones, biscuits and morning pancakes (until 14:00 in winter, 16:00 in summer). Order and pay at the counter, up to three items each. Slices of apple pie ¥784–1,111 to eat in. Cash only; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 平野顕子 · Founder and owner (Akiko Hirano in an October 2026 review), a cookery researcher · Kyoto · Per the official profile: born in Kyoto into a family of Noh-costume weavers; graduated from ノートルダム女学院 and, per the profile, an American university (named both 東コネチカット州立大学 and コネチカット大学 on the page); in 1995, while studying in New England, studied 17th-century New England baking under シャロル・ジーン; took a cake diploma, returned to Japan and opened cake classes, cafés and pantries in Kyoto and Tokyo; took a special lesson at the CIA in Hyde Park, New York, in April 2003; opened Cafe & Pantry 松之助 at Takakura, Kyoto, in October 2000. The name, unusual for a cake shop, is that of a grandfather who was a master Noh-costume craftsman. The official site lists a second shop, MATSUNOSUKE N.Y. in Daikanyama, Tokyo, and the book blurb there calls the owner the "Apple Pie Godmother". Tabelog Cafe "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022 and Cafe WEST 2025. · Sour cream apple pie; Big Apple Pie; pancakes.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free in practice: the menu is pies, cakes, scones, biscuits and pancakes, all wheat-based; no gluten-free item or allergen information is published (official menu).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the pies, cheesecakes and pancakes use butter, cream, sour cream, eggs and cheese (official menu; 2026 reviews). Drinks only.
places.hours: 9:00–17:30 (last order 17:00); closed Tuesday (open when a holiday), at Obon and New Year (Tabelog; official site). Pancakes 9:00–14:00 from October to March and 9:00–16:00 from April to September, until sold out (official site; Tabelog). No reservations for seats (Tabelog); order and pay at the co…

places.hood: Shimogamo-hondori by Shimogamo Shrine — 12 min walk from Demachiyanagi Stn
places.cu: Bakery of about 18 breads made from organic wheat (Waraku, 2022) · Toast Montagne, a loaf of 100% organic Canadian wheat (¥680 in 2022) · pain complet from organic whole wheat stone-milled in-house, naturally grown Hokkaido wheat blended in for about five years (Waraku, 2022) · baguette rouge, petit rouge ¥100, Fruity Levain with walnuts and organic figs ¥340, An with Tanba red beans ¥310, cinnam…
places.notes: [Bakery · Shimogamo, organic-wheat loaves by the shrine] A small wood-fitted bakery on Shimogamo-hondori next to Shimogamo Shrine, where one baker, 中川恵介, has made every loaf since opening. About 18 breads, from organic Canadian wheat and whole wheat stone-milled in the shop: the Toast Montagne loaf, a crusty baguette rouge, a fig-and-walnut levain (¥340), An with Tanba beans (¥310) and cinnamon walnut rolls (¥230). Takeaway only; come near the 10:00 opening, as breads sell out. Thursday–Sunday 10:00–16:00, cash only.
places.chef: 中川恵介 · Owner-baker, the only baker since opening (Waraku, 2022) · Per Waraku (magazine issue April/May 2022, republished online May 2024): since opening 13 years earlier, 中川恵介 alone has baked the bread in the workshop at the back; the shop makes 18 kinds; 100% organic Canadian wheat for the loaves, organic whole wheat stone-milled in-house for the pain complet, and about five years earlier began blending in naturally grown Hokkaido wheat; the baker says the slightly chewy texture suits Japanese tastes raised on rice. Tabelog Bread "Tabelog 100" 2017–2019 and Bread WEST 2020, 2022, 2026. · Per Waraku (2022): a chewy (もちっと) texture, which the baker thinks suits Japanese tastes raised on rice. · Toast Montagne; pain complet; baguette rouge.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a wheat bakery — organic Canadian wheat, in-house stone-milled organic whole wheat and Hokkaido wheat (Waraku, 2022).
places.vgd: Ask. No ingredient lists are published; reviewers note the rich butter of the croissant and pain au chocolat, and the An bread is filled with Tanba red beans (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Thursday–Sunday 10:00–16:00, until sold out; closed Monday–Wednesday (Tabelog; October 2026 reviews). Takeaway only (counter sales, 2026 reviews). The Toast Montagne loaf can be reserved by phone from 8:30 on the day (Waraku, 2022); a reviewer reserved loaves in person, paying in advance or on pick…

places.hood: Off Shinkyogoku, north of Shijo — 3 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Spanish bar with paella, ajillo and wine, open from noon (official site; Tabelog) · tapas from ¥500 (tortilla of the day), Iga mochi-pork roast ham, cheese, terrine, adult tuna salad, smoked mackerel with Brie, bonito marinated in balsamic · ajillo from ¥1,000 (shrimp and baby corn ¥1,100 in March 2026; Tanba shiitake and prosciutto) · paella: mussel and scampi ¥2,600, squid-ink arroz negro ¥2,80…
places.notes: [Spanish bar · Shinkyogoku, paella from noon] A small Spanish bar marked by a sign and a little window off Shinkyogoku, open since 2005: counter and tables downstairs, more tables upstairs, a three-seat terrace. Paella in small pans (scampi and mussel ¥2,600, squid ink ¥2,800), ajillos, Iga pork and a long by-the-glass wine list; lunch plates come with plenty of vegetables. A March 2026 diner found the squid-ink paella undercooked; others call it the highlight. 12:00–24:00, closed Wednesday; book for busy evenings.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed); a manager (店長) is mentioned on the official site · Tabelog gives the opening day as 1 April 2005 and notes the bar moved from Aburaya-cho on Takoyakushi-dori west of Fuyacho. The official site describes a hideaway Spanish bar marked by its sign and small window, with a red ceiling and wood inside, pairing wines from around the world with the food. The house bread uses Manitoba flour, Guérande salt, hard water and malt syrup at 100% hydration (official site). A July 2026 diner described two young staff as polite and quietly professional, matching the soft, gentle manner of the owner. · Paella; ajillo; balsamic-marinated bonito.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information. The menu leans on paella and ajillo, but ajillo comes with bread, the house bread is made with Manitoba wheat flour, and there are baked pastas and coca (Spanish flatbread pizza) (official menu; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. A vegetable tapas and leaf salad is on the menu, but the signature paella is cooked in a rich seafood stock based on prosciutto fat, and most dishes use pork, fish or cheese (official menu).
places.hours: Official site and Tabelog: 12:00–24:00 (food last order 23:00, drinks 23:30), closed Wednesday; tapas and paella can be ordered all day, 12:00–23:00. A March 2026 diner wrote that the bar opens at 15:00. Bookings online, by phone (075-213-0220) or through Tabelog; parties of 5 or more by phone; pri…

places.n: おばんざいと純洋食 アイサニ (Obanzai to Jun Youshoku Aisani)
places.hood: Nishi-Kiyamachi on the Takase River, north of Ayanokoji — near Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Kyoto obanzai and old-style yoshoku by the Takase River (official site) · obanzai ¥550 each (Kyoto-style okara, eggplant, yuba with greens, lotus root and celery kinpira, manganji pepper with jako), three for ¥920, five for ¥1,380 · Kyoto-style dashimaki ¥640, silken yuba ¥700, cream cheese cured in Saikyo miso ¥650, chicken liver with sansho ¥880, assorted Kyoto pickles ¥800 · yoshoku: demi-glac…
places.notes: [Obanzai & yoshoku · Takase River, a casual counter] A 16-seat counter and two sunken-kotatsu tables looking onto the Takase River in Nishi-Kiyamachi, open since October 2016; the name means "now and then" in Kyoto dialect, for a place people drop into now and then. Obanzai at ¥550 a dish (five for ¥1,380) laid out on the counter, plus yoshoku such as demi-glace hamburger steak and bifkatsu, and Kyoto sake. A five-kind sashimi plate was ¥980 in July 2026. One March 2026 visitor found it a little pricey for the food but loved the view. 17:00–23:00, closed Tuesday; book by phone.
places.chef: Master (マスター, unnamed on the official site) · The official site says the master aims for a casual shop that is easy to enter even alone, centred on Kyoto obanzai and nostalgic yoshoku, and explains the name as Kyoto dialect for "now and then", wishing guests would drop by now and then. It sits on the Takase River in Nishi-Kiyamachi, where the cherry trees bloom in spring. Tabelog gives the opening day as 14 October 2016; a September 2026 diner saw the 10th anniversary being celebrated and three friendly staff. · Per the official site: a casual shop, easy to enter even for one, centred on Kyoto obanzai and old-fashioned yoshoku. · Obanzai assortment; demi-glace hamburger steak; Kyoto sake.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information. The menu mixes Kyoto obanzai with yoshoku such as menchi-katsu, bifkatsu, a crab gratin and a demi-glace hamburger steak, plus fried dishes (tempura, kara-age) (official menu).
places.vgd: Ask. No vegan information. The obanzai include vegetable dishes (Kyoto-style okara, eggplant, yuba with greens, lotus root and celery kinpira), but several are simmered dishes (炊いたん) with no stock stated, and one has jako; the rest of the menu is meat and fish (official menu).
places.hours: Tabelog: 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00), closed Tuesday; hours may change; a July 2026 review gives the same and a June 2026 diner was told the shop stays open late at weekends. The official site still lists dinner 17:00–last order 20:30, closing 21:00, and opening 30 December–3 January. An October…

places.hood: Kawaramachi-dori south of Imadegawa — 5 min walk from Demachiyanagi Stn
places.cu: Kanmidokoro of homemade anmitsu and mamekan, with shaved ice in summer (Tabelog; Kansai Walker) · agar from Chiba tengusa seaweed, black syrup from Hateruma Island brown sugar, Hokkaido red peas and azuki, red-bean paste cooked each morning with a little salt, house-stewed apricots (Kansai Walker 2018, 2020; 2026 reviews) · shiratama anmitsu ¥800 (August 2026), matcha cream anmitsu, mamekan, toko…
places.notes: [Kanmi · Demachiyanagi, anmitsu and summer kakigori] A small table-only sweets shop on Kawaramachi-dori, marked by a noren reading "anmitsu": agar from Chiba tengusa, black syrup of Hateruma brown sugar, Hokkaido red peas and lightly salted red-bean paste, all made in the shop. Shiratama anmitsu ¥800; summer brings a thick house apricot ice and an Ippodo-hojicha shaved ice, winter zenzai. Expect a queue; cash only. Wagashi WEST Tabelog 100 2023 and 2026. 11:00–18:00 until sold out, closed Sunday and Monday.
places.chef: 松尾恵子 · Owner (店主, Kansai Walker 2020) · Kansai Walker (February 2020) quotes the owner, 松尾恵子: the black syrup of Okinawa Hateruma brown sugar is made with a stronger aroma and flavour so that it is not overpowered by the sea taste of the agar, and the plump Hokkaido red peas are popular. Kansai Walker (February 2018) adds agar slowly simmered from tengusa from the Chiba sea and red-bean paste cooked every morning with salt to hold down the sweetness. Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2019, 2020, 2022 and Wagashi WEST 2023, 2026. · Anmitsu; mamekan; apricot shaved ice.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information. The core sweets are agar jelly from tengusa seaweed, Hokkaido red peas and azuki, black syrup from Hateruma brown sugar, shiratama and house-stewed apricots (Kansai Walker 2020; 2026 reviews), but nothing is said about wheat or shared equipment; ice cream and kinako toppings are also served.
places.vgd: Ask. Anmitsu, mamekan and zenzai are built on agar, beans, brown-sugar syrup and rice dumplings, but cream versions, vanilla or matcha ice cream and a milk shaved ice are also on the menu (2026 reviews); no vegan information.
places.hours: Tabelog: Tuesday–Saturday 11:00–18:00 (last order 17:45), closed Sunday and Monday; open until sold out; hours may change (Tabelog; Kansai Walker 2020). No reservations; queues are common — one to eight groups on summer and autumn 2026 afternoons, a line before 10:45 on an August Saturday — and ord…

places.n: 祇園きなな 本店 (Gion Kinana Honten)
places.hood: Gion, a lane west of Hanamikoji — 7 min walk from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: Kinako ice cream café: "kinana" is ice cream of Tanba black-soybean kinako blended with domestic kinako, made without eggs, colourings or preservatives (official site) · freshly made kinana, served soft before it fully freezes, drink set ¥1,400; three-scoop set ¥1,600; parfaits with a drink — berry-berry kinana, kinana hapon (Japanese style: warabi mochi, shiratama, Tanba dainagon azuki, mugwort …
places.notes: [Kinako ice cream · Gion, upstairs off Hanamikoji] An upstairs café in a Gion townhouse lane serving kinana — ice cream of Tanba black-soybean kinako made without eggs or additives, served freshly made, soft and smooth, with hojicha or matcha (drink sets from ¥1,400). Parfaits pile it with warabi mochi, shiratama, yatsuhashi and mugwort or black-sesame ice. The owner first served it as the dessert at the restaurant 一碗, which has reopened downstairs as a six-seat counter. Cashless only; no children under 12. 12:00–18:00, irregular closures; booking recommended.
places.chef: 大本勝司 · Owner (店主, official site) · Per the owner’s greeting on the official site: more than 20 years ago the owner ran 一碗, a Kyoto restaurant shaped by the Slow Food idea, and the kinako ice cream served there after meals proved so popular that a sweets-only shop followed. The ice is made around the theme "gentle and delicious" with Tanba black-soybean kinako, no chemical colourings or preservatives, little fat and no eggs, so guests with egg allergy can eat it. The honten has 一碗 on the ground floor and the café upstairs. The 一碗 page (undated) says the shop had been in Gion 21 years when kinana was remade the previous autumn, with far fewer seats and bookings so guests no longer wait, and 味司一碗 reopened downstairs after 21 years: six counter seats, reservation only (Instagram DM), one omakase course ¥10,000. Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2018–2020, 2022 and Wagashi WEST 2026. · Per the official site: to keep serving ice cream that is truly gentle on the body and delicious, not something that looks good only because it is "Kyoto" or "Gion". · Freshly made kinana; kinana parfaits.
places.gfd: Ask. The kinako ice cream itself lists milk, cream, sugar, glucose, kinako (soy), skim milk powder, starch, agar and konjac flour (official site), but the parfaits add yatsuhashi, warabi mochi, rice-flour cookies and tiramisu (2026 reviews), and nothing is said about wheat in the starch or shared equipment.
places.vgd: Ask. The signature kinana ice cream is made with milk, cream and skim milk powder (official site), so the parfaits and sets are not vegan; it contains no egg. Ask about the shaved ice — the black-syrup kinako ice hides kinako ice cream inside (September 2026).
places.hours: Official site: 12:00–18:00 (last order 17:30); irregular closing days, posted on Instagram around the 20th of the month before. Tabelog instead gives 12:00–17:30, closed Thursday. places.notes: [Bistro · Ayanokoji, meat and wine in a townhouse] A neo-bistro in a townhouse just off the main streets between Karasuma and Kawaramachi — the "29" is niku, meat — with a counter, sofas and some 60 dishes that can all be ordered as halves: smoked mackerel on potato salad, sea urchin pudding with garlic toast, vine-smoked duck, 尾崎牛 beef from Miyazaki, game such as Ezo venison, then a hazelnut crème brûlée. Glass wines from ¥550, mostly French. ¥500 a head cover; most reviewers paid ¥3,000–10,000. Open 17:00–23:00; the site gives Tuesday as closed. Tabelog Bistro 100 2021.
places.chef: Chef (unnamed), trained at hotels in Japan and restaurants in France (Tabelog shop text) · Per the Tabelog shop text: authentic French cooking at fair prices by a chef who trained at renowned hotels in Japan and top restaurants in France, with a focus on meat. Per the official site: the shop first tasted 尾崎牛 at a nearby restaurant, wanted to know more, visited the farm and fell for the beef and its farmer; a counter was built to watch guests react; the wine list, chosen with a sommelier, describes each wine’s region, grape and character; the aim is hospitality that makes guests want to return. Opened 12 July 2011 (Tabelog). places.notes: [French & wine · Kiyamachi, a riverside platform and a sommelier] A 19-seat French restaurant at the Y-bend of the Takase River where you take off your shoes, sit at the counter or a table, and in summer move out to a platform over the Kamo River facing the Minami-za. The owner is a sommelier, and diners praise the glasses as much as the food: courses run from ¥9,350 (choose your main) to ¥23,000 with six paired glasses. In winter the house turns to mizutaki of Miyama chicken after French starters. Add ¥1,100 table charge and 10% service. Closed Sunday and the 2nd and 4th Monday.

places.cu: Gelato shop of BABBI, the Italian wafer maker with a 70-year history; the gelato uses its wafer pastes, alongside Japanese flavours such as matcha and black sesame (Tabelog) · pistachio, hazelnut, chocolate, ricotta fig, rich milk, salted caramel vanilla, Amaou strawberry, yuzu and lemon, cookies and cream, black sesame, cherry (2024–26 reviews) · cup, wafer or cocoa cone topped with a BABBI wafe…
places.notes: [Gelato · Kiyamachi, Italian gelato over the Kamo River] The only gelato shop of BABBI, the Italian wafer brand, at the Dango Bridge end of Kiyamachi: flavours from pistachio and hazelnut to ricotta fig and Kyoto-leaning matcha and black sesame, in a cup or a cone crowned with a BABBI wafer. Eat inside looking at the river, or from May to October on the riverside platform, where prices run higher (a single was ¥990 there in August 2026). Open daily 13:00–22:00, a handy stop after dinner in Kiyamachi.
places.chef: Shop of the Italian brand BABBI, run in Japan by a company (corporate invoice registrant, Tabelog); no staff named · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): a gelato shop from the Italian wafer brand BABBI, which has a 70-year history, using its wafer pastes in the gelato and offering Japanese flavours such as matcha and black sesame; it faces the Kamo River. Walkerplus (February 2020) reported it as the brand’s first gelato shop in Japan; an October 2026 reviewer says it is still the only BABBI location in Japan serving gelato, with ingredients imported from Italy and made in-house, and a September 2026 reviewer notes BABBI also has a Tokyo shop. · Pistachio and hazelnut gelato; wafer-topped cones.

places.notes: [Negiyaki · Gion, a teppan counter by Yasaka Shrine] A 12-seat counter on Higashioji-dori near Yasaka Shrine, founded in 1984 per a reviewer, where the owner cooks on the teppan in front of you and chats with the regulars along the counter. Order the negiyaki — thin batter under a heap of green onion, with soy sauce (¥800 with pork) — or the Kyoto betayaki with its spicy sauce, and start with the special dashimaki rolled on the griddle with pickled ginger (¥650) while you wait. Book ahead; two-hour limit; cash only. Open until 3:00 on Friday and Saturday; closed Monday.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Pontocho, obanzai and hot pot until 2 am] A large, bright second-floor izakaya on Pontocho with Japanese umbrellas hanging from the ceiling, open from mid-afternoon (noon at weekends) to 2:00 every day: Kyoto obanzai like yuba sashimi and eggplant in dashi, a pork-offal-and-clam hot pot, and Kyoto and Shiga sake, mostly as all-you-can-drink courses (¥5,000–6,000). Easy to book even on the day. Reviews are mixed; many guests are tourists.

Phone ahead — booked orders come first, and fresh sweets need a day's notice; walk-ins often find things sold out. Tabelog says it is under renovation and taking phone orders. Cash only.

Tabelog Japanese-sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026, Sweets WEST 2018–2020 and 2022, Sweets 2017. · Mikasa; monaka; seasonal jō-namagashi.

A three-beer, three-dish tasting set (¥2,500) is the easy way in. Reviewers like the beer and the panna cotta; two found the high chairs uncomfortable, and some found the prices on the high side. English menu. Open from noon at weekends; closed Tuesday.

places.notes: [Chicken · Shijo Kawabata, a 10-seat chicken counter by the Kamo River] A narrow ten-seat counter on Kawabata-dori just north of Shijo, where the master grills chicken and quail over charcoal and serves it off the skewer in bite-size pieces. Start with the chicken sashimi — white liver with sesame oil, heart, kombu-cured breast — or the rare thigh tataki; then quail thigh, gizzard, red liver and grilled vegetables such as Kamo eggplant; finish with an oyakodon soaked in dashi. Good sake, including Aramasa. Almost always full: book, or ask for an hour's slot. Bills ran about ¥6,000–15,000 a head in 2026. Closed Wednesday.

A regular of ten years (January 2024) and others describe it as always booked. Tabelog Chicken "Tabelog 100" 2025. · Chicken sashimi (white liver); thigh tataki; oyakodon.

places.notes: [Bar & kakigori · Kiyamachi, Ginza's Star Bar in a Kyoto alley] The Kyoto branch of Ginza's Star Bar, down an alley between Kiyamachi and Pontocho: a dim, Japanese-styled room with a tea set at its centre, where the kimono-clad master works alone. Everything turns on ice — hand-cut clear ice for highballs, and the bar's own 洛氷 from Kyoto spring water, shaved into kakigori (¥2,500) with matcha whisked at the counter or yuzu syrup. Come before 19:00 to skip the ¥2,200 table charge. Cocktails run ¥2,000–3,000. Cards only. One May 2026 visitor found the charge poor value and the staff absorbed in a computer.
places.chef: 松田 高雅 · Owner (the invoice holder); a May 2026 review describes the master, in a kimono, managing everything solo · Per Tabelog: a directly managed shop of STAR BAR GINZA in Ginza 1-chome, Tokyo. Per the official site: four STAR BAR shops (Ginza, Namiki, Kyoto, Hibiya Midtown); Star Bar made ice the star of the bar, uses three kinds of ice frozen in different ways, and the Kyoto shop makes craft ice (洛氷) from Kyoto spring waters under the only ice-making licence in Kyoto city; by day in summer the Kyoto shop is a kakigori shop. The invoice register lists an individual, 松田 高雅, for the Kyoto shop’s invoice number. Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022. Opened 11 July 2016. · Per the official site: hand-cut ice is pursued for function as well as beauty, down to water quality and the theory of freezing. · Kakigori of 洛氷; matcha cocktails; hand-cut ice.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Kiyamachi, a 1928 ryotei famous for suppon] A sukiya-style ryotei between the Takase River and the Kamo, founded in 1928 by 栗栖 熊三郎 at a five-seat counter and now run by the family's fourth generation, Junichi Kurisu (from September 2026), a sommelier who travelled some 80 countries. The kaiseki is 'monmo' — ingredients served as they are — and its signature is suppon, in the 丸吸 soup or the 丸鍋 hot pot. It was among the first Kyoto ryotei with halal certification (2014) and serves kosher and vegan kaiseki on request. Courses from ¥22,000 plus 15% service; riverside kawadoko in summer. Booking required; closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Teppan steak · Gion Shirakawa, a beef house since 1929] A third-generation beef house on the Shirakawa, where the cooks grill only female wagyu — bought whole, aged and boned in-house — on the teppan in front of a 16-seat counter, with big windows onto weeping cherries in spring and greenery in summer. Steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki come together in the ¥30,000 three-way course; the lunch steak starts at ¥5,000 for 100 g. The house began teppan steak after the war at the request of occupation officers. Formal dress; book ahead; closed Monday.
places.chef: 三田兼司 (third generation) · Third-generation owner (official site) · Per the official site: founded in 1929 (Showa 4) — Tabelog’s shop text gives 1927 — as a gyūnabe house that grew on the founder 三田進太郎’s "太牢油焼"; teppan steak began after the war at the request of occupation officers; the founder, the second generation 三田昌治 and the third generation 三田兼司 have served only the best cuts of female cattle; calves registered by nose print and raised in Sanda, Hyogo, are bought whole and aged and boned in the shop; the centenary falls in 2029. A sister shop, 北新地みかく, is in Osaka (official site; a June 2026 reviewer also mentions it). · Per the official site: choose the finest beef, cut it with the best technique and cook it to the best doneness, unchanged since the founder. · Three-way course of steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki.
places.gfd: Ask. Teppan steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki, finished with garlic rice or Mikaku beef curry; sukiyaki and curry usually involve soy sauce or roux, and no gluten information is given (official menu; 2024–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a beef house; even the lunch comes with beef shigure on the rice and a beef-bone soup (official menu).
places.hours: Lunch 12:00–14:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Monday; booking required for both (official site). Tabelog adds that dinner should be booked a day or two ahead. Formal dress: no sandals or patterned shirts in summer; school-age children only, no infants (Tabelog)…

places.n: トラットリア レオーネ (Trattoria Leone)
places.hood: Takatsuji-dori west of Muromachi, south of Shijo Karasuma — 5–10 min walk from Shijo Stn
places.cu: Authentic Tuscan cooking in a small trattoria (Tabelog shop text) · lunch, four set options from salad and pasta to appetisers, pasta, main and dessert: salad and the day’s spaghetti ¥1,300 (September 2026); a generous appetiser platter of frittata, bean stew, fritters, crostini with chicken-liver pâté and a small lasagna (July–October 2026) · pastas: spicy spaghetti carrettiera, homemade pappard…
places.notes: [Italian · Shijo Karasuma, a small Tuscan trattoria] A 16-seat trattoria south of Shijo Karasuma, open since 2007, with maps and drawings on the walls and cooking straight from Tuscany: an appetiser platter so large it is nearly a meal, spicy carrettiera, homemade pappardelle with wagyu ragù, herb-roasted arista and chicken-liver crostini, with Tuscan wines from about ¥3,000 a bottle. Lunch from ¥1,300 is a bargain and fills up — book by phone. Service is quiet and minimal: reviewers in June and October 2026 found it brusque and unexplained. Closed Wednesday and the third Tuesday. Tabelog Italian WEST 100 2021.
places.chef: Chef and a server (unnamed in the sources) · Per the Tabelog shop text: a cozy little Italian restaurant of authentic Tuscan cuisine. Opened 11 November 2007 (Tabelog). Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. Regulars in 2026 praise the value and the portions; two 2026 reviewers describe a quiet server who explains little. · Tuscan appetiser platter; carrettiera; wagyu ragù pappardelle; arista.
places.gfd: Ask. Tuscan trattoria: pasta (dried and homemade), lasagna, crostini, arancini and breaded vegetables in the appetiser platter, bread with meals; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. A vegetable aglio e olio and basil pasta appear as daily pastas, but the appetiser platters mix in tuna, liver, omelette and cheese; no vegan dish is named (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 12:00–14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner 18:00–22:00 (last order 21:00); closed Wednesday and the third Tuesday of the month (Tabelog). Book by phone: Tabelog takes one online booking (up to two people) a day and none for Friday to Sunday; lunch booking advised (Tabelog; July 2026). No children…

places.n: The Churrasco 京都河原町 (The Churrasco Kyoto Kawaramachi)
places.hood: Kawaramachi-dori south of Takoyakushi, 6th floor — 2 min walk from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: All-you-can-eat Brazilian churrasco: skewers of beef, pork, chicken and sausage roasted with rock salt and carved at the table, plus grilled vegetables, grilled pineapple, pão de queijo, a salad bar, curry and rice (Tabelog shop text; 2026 reviews) · courses (2 hours): premium, 18 churrasco types and Italian dishes ¥4,990; standard, 16 types ¥3,990 (Tabelog); a reviewer paid ¥4,490 for the standa…
places.notes: [Churrasco · Kawaramachi, all-you-can-eat Brazilian grill] A big, 100-seat churrasco room on the 6th floor of the Don Quijote at Shijo Kawaramachi, with night views over the city: staff — one reviewer mentions a Brazilian chef — carve skewers of beef, garlic chicken and sausage at the table, with grilled pineapple, cheese bread, a salad bar and a well-liked curry. Two-hour courses run ¥3,990–4,990 (more on Sundays and in late December); there is also an Italian buffet with free drinks for ¥3,500. Good for groups and families. One October 2026 regular found the beef tough and the carving clumsy. Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST 100 2026.
places.chef: Staff who carve at the table; a Brazilian chef per one review (October 2026) · Per the Tabelog shop text: one of the few churrasco restaurants in Kyoto, with all-you-can-eat and all-you-can-drink courses, wagyu skewers grilled and carved in front of you, and a night view; projector and microphone hire for groups. The operator’s website is will-food.com (株式会社WILL). Tabelog gives the opening date as 1 May 2025, while its shop text says "Opened in May 2023". Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026. · Churrasco skewers carved at the table; grilled pineapple.
places.gfd: Ask. Grilled meats carved at the table with sauces, alongside a buffet of bread, curry, pizza, pasta and fried dishes; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: an all-you-can-eat meat restaurant; grilled vegetables, pineapple and the salad bar are sides (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Monday to Friday 16:00–23:30; Saturday 12:00–23:00; Sunday and holidays 12:00–23:30; last food order 22:30, drinks 23:00 (Tabelog). Two-hour sittings (food last order at 70 or 90 minutes, depending on the course); one drink per person unless you take free drinks (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, sa…
