places.hood: Back alley behind Fujii Daimaru, Shijo Teramachi — 2 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Izakaya in a renovated townhouse: fish grilled over straw, teppanyaki, seasonal dishes and seasonal sake, including Kyoto sakes such as Shōtendōji and Hōryō (Tabelog, shop text) · Manzoku course of 7 dishes with straw-grilled seasonal seafood ¥5,000 (Tabelog) · straw-grilled platter, sashimi with seared bonito, sea urchin, grilled squid, grilled hokke, katsuobushi shuto (2026 reviews) · warm pota…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo Teramachi, straw-grilled fish in a townhouse] A renovated Kyoto townhouse at the end of an alley behind Fujii Daimaru, with a busy counter downstairs and tables upstairs. The house specialty is fish seared over burning straw — try the straw-grilled platter or the ¥5,000 seven-dish course — alongside a much-praised warm potato salad, shrimp mayo with corn, fried corn and, in the cold months, oden. Kyoto sakes by the season. Some 2026 diners found service slow, especially upstairs where you ring a bell. Book ahead; open daily 18:00–24:00.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed in the sources) · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): an adult hideaway renovated from a Kyoto townhouse, with fish grilled over straw and sizzling teppanyaki made from seasonal ingredients, and seasonal sake; the owner wants every guest to try the signature straw-grilled dish in the Manzoku course. An October 2026 reviewer found the counter busy with many international customers; another that month noted a wide age range among the patrons. · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): dishes that highlight the natural flavours of the ingredients. · Straw-grilled seafood; warm potato salad; oden.
places.gfd: Ask. Straw-grilled fish, teppanyaki and oden with soy-based seasonings, plus fried dishes (fried oysters, shrimp mayo, fried corn) and hamburg steak; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and grilled vegetables are on the menu, but the oden is in broth and most dishes are fish, chicken or beef (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–24:00 daily; last booking for dining 21:00; closed irregularly (Tabelog). Book ahead, especially at weekends; on-the-day bookings and cancellations sometimes free a seat (October 2026). places.hood: Teramachi-dori north of Nishiki, basement — 3 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Large teppan izakaya of black-wagyu steak grilled on the teppan and in a stone oven, served on warming trays, with Kyoto obanzai (Tabelog, shop text) · lunch: a plate of eight obanzai with a main — wagyu steak, ginger pork, beef short rib, chicken nanban — and free refills of homemade steamed tofu, multigrain rice and miso soup; from about ¥1,000, over ¥2,000 with beef short rib (September 2026) …
places.notes: [Steak & obanzai · Teramachi, wagyu and all-you-can-eat tofu] A big, lively basement restaurant on Teramachi near Nishiki Market, the main shop of a small Kyoto group, where black wagyu is seared on the teppan and finished in a stone oven. Lunch is the draw: eight small obanzai, a main of steak or ginger pork, and unlimited refills of warm homemade tofu, multigrain rice and miso soup, from about ¥1,000. Evenings bring steak, dashimaki and a tower of frozen-lemon sour, with the tofu as a ¥330 starter. Some 2026 diners found dishes salty or a fried dish served cold. Open daily.
places.chef: Company-run restaurant (a corporate invoice registrant, Tabelog); no staff named · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): steaks grilled on a teppan and in a stone oven, served with warming trays; homemade steamed tofu refilled at lunch and as the dinner starter; Kyoto obanzai lunches; room for banquets of 30 or more. Other 市場小路 shops: AEON Mall Kitaoji (Gurunavi) and Katsuragawa (an August 2026 reviewer who visits all three). · Stone-oven wagyu steak; obanzai lunch with unlimited tofu.
places.gfd: Ask. Steaks are grilled on the teppan and in a stone oven, but sauces, obanzai, chicken nanban and tofu toppings use soy and other seasonings; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and the homemade tofu, multigrain rice and some obanzai may suit, but dashi and miso soup are likely and the mains are meat (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–16:00 (last order 15:00), dinner 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:15); closed on New Year’s Day (Tabelog). places.cu: Bakery with a wood-fired clay oven (2026 reviews) · walnut bread ¥90 (June 2026), raisin and orange bread ¥90, whole-wheat sesame chocolate bread ¥160, つぶあんぱん ¥220, hazelnut "Sunrise" ¥250, チョコクロワッサン ¥250 (September 2026), orange croissant ¥250 (April 2026) · yama-shokupan loaves sliced to order, cream buns, bread with Lindenbaum sausage, dried-fruit rusk (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Bakery · Kojinguchi, one baker and a wood-fired oven] A tiny bakery on Kawaramachi-dori where the owner bakes alone in a large clay oven fired with wood, and prices stay low — a walnut bread is ¥90. Come near the 11:00 opening: the walnut bread and the hazelnut 'Sunrise' go fast, and by late afternoon little may be left. Loaves are sliced as you like. Takeaway only, cash only. Tuesday–Saturday; closed all of August.
places.chef: Owner-baker who runs the shop alone (unnamed in the sources) · Per a July 2026 reviewer: the owner and a friend designed the interior and built a large clay oven fired with thinned wood from the mountains of Kyoto (the same review mentions firewood from Miyama); the name means "goodwill" in French; as the sole baker, the owner’s baking times and quantities vary from day to day. A June 2026 reviewer also notes the single staff member. A November 2026 visitor came on the recommendation of several geiko but found it closed on Sunday. Tabelog Bread WEST "Tabelog 100" 2020, 2022, 2026. · Walnut bread; hazelnut Sunrise; yama-shokupan.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a wheat bakery — loaves, croissants, filled buns and rusks (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Plain loaves and walnut or raisin breads may be simple doughs, but croissants, cream buns and sausage bread are not, and no ingredient lists are published (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tuesday–Saturday 11:00–20:00; closed Sunday, Monday and all of August; times may change with the baking (Tabelog; September 2026). Popular breads, especially the walnut bread, can sell out soon after opening or before it, and the shelves can be nearly empty by 16:00 (June–July 2026). Phone reservat…

places.hood: Okazaki near the Kyoto City Zoo — 7 min walk from Keage Stn
places.cu: Cake shop with a retro upstairs tea room (2026 reviews) · summer kakigori, served with warm hojicha: pudding kakigori with custard, caramel and a whole pudding inside ¥1,400; matcha and Uji matcha, mango, peach, strawberry (June–September 2026) · cakes: cube-shaped cheesecake on a lemon white-chocolate cookie base, donut-shaped tiramisu with coffee jelly and Japanese chestnut Mont Blanc, about ¥6…
places.notes: [Cake shop & tea room · Okazaki, pudding kakigori] A small cake shop near the Kyoto City Zoo with a Showa-retro tea room upstairs. In summer it is all kakigori — the pudding kakigori (¥1,400), with custard, caramel and a whole pudding hidden inside, is the one people queue for; the rest of the year you pick a cake downstairs (donut-shaped tiramisu, chestnut Mont Blanc, cube cheesecake, about ¥600) and eat it upstairs with coffee. Expect to wait outside, one group at a time. No photos inside; cash only. Wednesday–Sunday 10:00–18:00.
places.chef: Cake shop; no one is named in the sources · Reviewers in 2026 describe a small cake shop near the zoo with a retro, Showa-era feel, a tea room upstairs that serves kakigori from about May to September, careful choice of furniture and decor, and a no-photography rule. Tabelog Cafe "Tabelog 100" 2022 and Cafe WEST 2025. · Pudding kakigori; tiramisu; Mont Blanc.
places.gfd: Ask. Kakigori and pudding are flour-free in principle, but the cakes (cheesecake on a cookie base, tiramisu, Mont Blanc) use wheat, and no ingredient lists are published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Fruit and matcha kakigori syrups may be plant-based, but the pudding kakigori, custard and the cakes use milk, cream and eggs; no ingredient lists are published (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Wednesday–Sunday 10:00–18:00, until sold out; closed Monday and Tuesday (Tabelog). No reservations; cash only (Tabelog). Order on the ground floor, then sit in the upstairs tea room and pay on leaving (2026 reviews). Kakigori is served upstairs from about May to September, when cakes are takeaway o…

places.cu: Izakaya for Kyoto vegetables, obanzai, fish and sake (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · stone-grilled and steamed Kyoto vegetables, Manganji peppers, Kujo green onion stir-fried with chicken neck · assorted obanzai, simmered pork belly and taro, fried Kyoto yuba, the house tofu (one reviewer’s "best ever") · thick-cut sashimi, hamo with sauce, tempura with three salts · curry udon to finish · all-you-can-…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo-Tominokoji, Kyoto vegetables until 1 am] A second-floor izakaya up a steep stair just north of Shijo, open until 1:00 every night: stone-grilled and steamed Kyoto vegetables, obanzai, a house tofu that reviewers rave about, thick-cut sashimi and local sake, with curry udon to finish. Bills about ¥5,000–8,000 a head; an all-you-can-drink course is ¥6,000. One of three Sumika shops in Kyoto. Smoking allowed.
places.chef: Operator unnamed in the sources · Opened 22 August 2009 (Tabelog). Our crawl lists two other 棲家 shops in Kyoto, the 本店 (Tabelog 26004942) and the 三条店 (26030888). · Kyoto vegetables; obanzai; house tofu.
places.gfd: Ask. Obanzai, simmered dishes and vegetables built on dashi, plus tempura, fried yuba and curry udon; the shop asks guests to tell it about allergies, but no gluten information is given (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the menu is rich in Kyoto vegetables and tofu, but the obanzai and simmered dishes use dashi, and the courses include fish and pork (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Monday–Friday 18:00–1:00, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 17:00–1:00 (last order 0:30); closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Bookings for seats only; stays may be limited to two hours when busy; tell the shop about allergies (Tabelog). All-you-can-drink course ¥6,000 (September 2026). 34 seats: 6 at the…

places.hood: East of the Kamo River near the Minamiza, north of Shijo — 3 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: Casual Japanese kaiseki and à la carte: market-fresh fish, obanzai, seasonal flavours and dashi (Tabelog) · omakase course with seasonal clay-pot rice (Tabelog) · à la carte: sashimi platters, battera, firefly-squid shabu-shabu in spring, oysters and ayu in early summer, matsutake in autumn · "today’s kamadaki rice" from three choices, e.g. with eel; leftovers made into onigiri to take home · sea…
places.notes: [Japanese · Gion-Shijo, à la carte by the counter] A second-floor Japanese restaurant near the Minamiza, opened in 2023, with a long counter staffed by several cooks and a few private rooms. Order a little of everything — market fish, seasonal shabu-shabu, battera — with sake matched by the staff, and finish with kamadaki rice (leftovers come back as onigiri). About ¥10,000–15,000 a head; portions are small. Open late; closed Sunday.
places.chef: Chef (unnamed in the sources) · Opened 15 January 2023 (Tabelog). Per the operator’s Tabelog text: freshness first in the sashimi, easy obanzai, seasonal flavours and dashi; fish bought directly from the market. · Seasonal fish; kamadaki rice.
places.gfd: Ask. Seasonal Japanese à la carte with an emphasis on dashi — sashimi, grilled and fried dishes, battera, clay-pot rice; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan in practice: the menu centres on market fish and dashi-based cooking (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: 17:30–23:30 (last order 23:00), Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday and public holidays (Tabelog). Bookings online or by phone; five or more by phone (Tabelog). 18 seats: a long counter and private rooms for 4–8; smoking area until 21:00; BYO allowed; cards accepted (Tabelog; January 2026). places.n: ドミニク・ブシェ・キョート・ル・テッパンヤキ (Dominique Bouchet Kyoto Le Teppanyaki)
places.hood: Keage, in The Westin Miyako Kyoto — 2 min from Keage Stn
places.cu: Teppanyaki with French touches, the first teppanyaki restaurant produced by the French chef Dominique Bouchet (official site) · French-style appetizers and desserts; Kyoto-raised beef and brand wagyu — Kobe, Omi and Kyoto beef, A4 grade or higher, offered as a three-way comparison (official site) · lunch from ¥10,000, dinner from ¥20,000 (official site) · seasonal grilled vegetables, abalone, blu…
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · Keage, a French chef’s grill in The Westin Miyako] The Westin Miyako’s teppanyaki room, produced by the French chef Dominique Bouchet: counter rooms for six to eight with views over Higashiyama, French-style starters and desserts, then Kobe, Omi and Kyoto wagyu, abalone and lobster on the plate, and garlic rice or lobster ramen to finish. Lunch from ¥10,000, dinner from ¥20,000. Book lunch the day before; jacket suggested. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Dominique Bouchet · Producing chef (監修, per the hotel’s page); the teppan chefs are not named · Poitou-Charentes, France (hotel page). · Per the hotel page: born in Poitou-Charentes; head chef at La Tour d’Argent and Hôtel de Crillon in Paris before opening Restaurant Dominique Bouchet in Paris’s 8th arrondissement in 2004; besides Kyoto, now runs Dominique Bouchet Tokyo in Ginza and the bistro Les Copains de Dominique Bouchet. This is the first teppanyaki restaurant Bouchet has produced. Opened 27 November 2019 (Tabelog). Tabelog Steak/Teppanyaki WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025. The same hotel also houses Dominique Bouchet Kyoto Le Restaurant (hotel page). · Per the hotel page: a new kind of teppanyaki with French playfulness. · Wagyu teppanyaki; garlic rice; lobster ramen.
places.gfd: Ask. Teppanyaki courses of wagyu, seafood and grilled vegetables with French sauces and appetizers, garlic rice or ramen to finish; no gluten information (official site; 2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the courses are built on wagyu, lobster and abalone, with sauces such as beef rillettes and butter (official site; 2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–14:30, dinner 17:00–22:00 (last entry 20:00); closed Wednesday except holidays; lunch must be booked by 20:00 the day before (official site). Lunch from ¥10,000, dinner from ¥20,000, tax and service included (official site); Tabelog lists a 15% service charge. Changes and cancellations …

places.hood: Imadegawa-dori by Kyoto University, east of Hyakumanben — 2 min from the Kyoto University…
places.cu: Patisserie and bakery with a small café (Tabelog) · cakes: Earl Grey mousse, peach tart ¥640, cheese tart, "master roll" cake · breads: baguette, curry bread · kakigori in season, e.g. pistachio-muscat, raspberry, mango, and the Caramel Mocha "Satopetino" with espuma and coffee jelly ¥1,300 · iced latte ¥440, homemade lemonade (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Patisserie · Kitashirakawa by Kyoto University] A small patisserie-bakery on Imadegawa near Kyoto University, opened in 2016 by Kyoto-born pâtissier Tatsuhito Satoi, formerly sous-chef at Sweets Garden Yuji Ajiki in Yokohama: refined cakes and tarts (peach tart ¥640), bread, and in the warm months mountainous kakigori with espuma (about ¥1,300). Nine seats inside. Open daily 8:00–17:00; pay by PayPay or au PAY.
places.chef: Tatsuhito Satoi · Owner-pâtissier (Tabelog remarks; October 2026 review) · Kyoto (home town, per an October 2026 review). · Per Tabelog: a patisserie opened by Satoi, a staff member who supported Yuji Ajiki from the start. Per an October 2026 review: previously sous-chef at Sweets Garden Yuji Ajiki in Yokohama, returned to home-town Kyoto and opened the shop in 2016. Opened 15 April 2016 (Tabelog). Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026. · Cakes; seasonal kakigori.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free in practice: cakes, tarts, roll cakes and a bakery line (baguette, curry bread); the kakigori comes with espuma, jellies and sauces whose ingredients are not published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Cakes, mousses and kakigori espuma use dairy or eggs; plain breads and fruit-sauce kakigori may suit, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 8:00–17:00 every day, with occasional temporary closures; kakigori and parfaits 11:00–16:00 (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). 9 seats at a counter and a few tables at the back (Tabelog; August 2026). PayPay and au PAY only; no cards (Tabelog). On Imadegawa-dori between Hyakumanben and Ginkakuji…

places.n: 焼き鳥 参 木屋町店 (umaimonyaki sun Kiyamachi Ten)
places.hood: An alley off Kiyamachi north of Shijo — 3 min from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Yakitori over binchotan with locally sourced chicken, plus vegetables bought daily (October 2025) · 10-skewer assortment; skewers such as neck, gizzard, heart, tsukune, negima, shiso-wrapped neck and breast, quail eggs, shiitake (2024–2026 reviews) · "lard rice", the house signature (October 2025) · fried bonjiri, young-chicken kara-age, fried cartilage · avocado with house chili oil, eggplant de…
places.notes: [Yakitori · Kiyamachi, binchotan skewers and lard rice down an alley] A two-storey yakitori house down a narrow alley off Kiyamachi: counter and tables below, tatami and sofa seats up a steep stair. The skewers are grilled over binchotan, the vegetables come in daily — raw ones with a spicy miso dip, eggplant dengaku, lotus-root chijimi — and the thing to finish with is the "lard rice". Order by QR code; English menus. Most reviews praise the skewers and the staff; an April 2024 visitor found the service cold and rushed. Open nightly 18:00–24:00.
places.chef: Operator not named (Tabelog lists an invoice number) · An October 2025 reviewer describes the yakitori as grilled over binchotan from fresh, locally sourced chicken, with vegetables sourced daily, and the "lard rice" as featured in a famous restaurant guide. · Binchotan yakitori; lard rice; vegetable dishes.

places.chef: 三嶋太郎 · Fifth-generation head (五代目主人), per the official site · Per the official site: the founder 三嶌兼吉, who served a court-noble’s samurai, learned gyunabe in Nagasaki together with the founder’s wife てい and opened Mishima Tei here on Teramachi-Sanjo in Meiji 6 (1873); the sukiya interior — garden, railings, ceilings, lattices — is mostly as it was at the founding; the house selects black wagyu from across Japan regardless of origin and ages it in its own way, cooking the sukiyaki on electric heaters that act like charcoal. The fifth generation, 三嶋太郎, refined the secret warishita, began training in Japanese cuisine, tea and ikebana eight years before the page was written, and devised the kaiseki-style Hana course with appetisers, sweets and usucha. A sister restaurant, 翁樹庵, is introduced on the site. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2019; Hot Pot "Tabelog 100" 2024 and 2026. · Per the official site: keeping the good things of old Kyoto, which is now harder than making new ones; the fifth generation aims to keep evolving while carrying on the tradition. · Sukiyaki of black wagyu with the house warishita.

Also kintsuba, chestnut sweets and seasonal fresh sweets. Closed Wednesday and some Thursdays.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Nishijin, a 300-year-old ryotei of court cuisine] A ryotei on Inokuma-dori in Nishijin that began in 1722 as a sake brewery, 萬屋, and later became the restaurant 萬亀楼; it formally carries on the Imperial Court's Ikama-ryu ceremonial knife school and yusoku-ryori, and the present head is the tenth generation. Meals are served in private tatami rooms over a garden: seasonal courses with hamo and live-grilled ayu in summer, crab and karasumi in winter, and a kago bento at lunch. Courses run about ¥30,000–40,000 a head with about 20% added; at events there may be shikibocho and maiko. Book ahead.

places.notes: [French · Kawaramachi-Takatsuji, a seafood French in the attic] A twelve-seat attic restaurant west of Kawaramachi-Takatsuji, decorated after the sea of the south of France and of the owner-chef's home, where Shingo Giki cooks French food built on Japanese seafood. places.notes: [Yakitori & oyakodon · Gion Shirakawa, a Meiji chicken family's casual shop] The casual counter of 鳥新, a Gion chicken house whose family traces itself to the mid-Meiji era and whose earlier shops appear in Ryōma ga Yuku and Tanizaki. At lunch it serves only oyakodon — the old geisha-delivery recipe, egg set round a raw yolk with Kujo onion on Tsuruga rice, with house pickles and miso soup; at night, a ¥2,200 skewer omakase with chicken soup. Cash only; smoking allowed; closed Thursday.
places.chef: Owner, fourth generation by the family’s count (official site); unnamed · Per the official site of 鳥新: founded about 120 years ago in the mid-Meiji era, with the present owner "said to be the fourth generation" though without firm proof; related 鳥新 shops once stood by Shijo Kobashi, on Kawaramachi, Teramachi and Shinkyogoku, and the family traces bird dealing back to Oda Nobunaga’s time; the Shijo Kobashi shop is thought to be the one in the last scene of Shiba Ryōtarō’s "Ryōma ga Yuku"; Tanizaki Jun’ichirō wrote of the Teramachi shop (Bungei Shunjū, 1924) and ate at Nawate; mizutaki came to dominate over sukiyaki from about Showa 40. The oyakodon was made for delivery to geiko, maiko and Gion households from the late Meiji, delivery ended around 1955, and the dish was revived for lunch at とり新 after some fifty years (official site). An August 2025 reviewer found the owner a person of few words who wore very tall geta; an April 2026 reviewer calls the house Meiji-era. · Per the official site: "町の普通の店" — an ordinary neighbourhood shop, a secret little space in Kyoto. · Oyakodon; yakitori omakase.

places.notes: [Ryokan kaiseki · Fuyacho, one of Kyoto's grand old inns] A historic inn near Oike, in the inn trade since 1861 (the house since 1818), whose holly crest is on everything and whose guests have included Kawabata Yasunari: seasonal Kyoto kaiseki in your room or a dining room, with fine old tableware. You can come just to eat — dinner for two or more, lunch for groups of ten — by booking ahead; allergies and vegetarian requests need three days' notice. Expect ¥20,000–50,000 a head. A 2026 Michelin Key hotel and Relais & Châteaux member.

places.notes: [French · Marutamachi, Chef Alexey Moko's townhouse] A modern French restaurant in a renovated Kyoto townhouse with a central counter, a courtyard and a storehouse, where Chef Alexey Moko — trained at Taillevent and in London hotels — cooks Japanese ingredients aged and fermented in-house: week-aged fish with koji or sourdough-miso sauces, game, and a sourdough loaf with butter people ask for again and again. Lunch ¥9,000, dinner ¥22,000, with natural-wine pairings. Families welcome, with a kids' menu. Michelin one star, per reviewers. Closed Sunday and Monday.

Tabelog records eight straight years of a Bib Gourmand. Book ahead; dinner Tuesday–Sunday, lunch at weekends.

places.notes: [Wagashi · Nishi Hongan-ji, the matsukaze of a 600-year-old confectioner] An old confectioner opposite Nishi Hongan-ji that by its own history has supplied the temple's offerings since 1421. Its famous 松風 is a chewy, bread-like slab of fermented wheat dough, white miso and malt syrup, baked in a huge pan and scattered with poppy seeds — said to have started as siege rations in the 石山合戦, and named from a poem by 顕如. Eight pieces ¥700; cut-end bags are a bargain. Seasonal wagashi are sold only here. Takeaway only; 8:30–17:00, closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 株式会社亀屋陸奥 (founded as a company in 1964; official site); no person is named in the sources read · Per the official site: founded, by tradition, in 1421; supplier of offerings to Hongan-ji from about the time 蓮如 (Rennyo) led it; during the 石山合戦 (from 1570) a sweet first made as rations became matsukaze, named after 顕如’s poem once Hongan-ji settled at 六条堀川 (1591); around 1660 the house received a cypress turtle said to have floated in Hideyoshi’s Jurakudai pond, the 亀 of its name, and in 1715 the title 陸奥大掾 from the court; matsukaze specimens won silver at the 1900 Paris Exposition; incorporated in 1964. 司馬遼太郎 wrote matsukaze into 『燃えよ剣』 and 『関ヶ原』. Tabelog Wagashi WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026 (official site news, 29 September 2026). · Per the official site: to keep the taste handed down since the Warring States period and pass it on to the next era, one sheet at a time. · 松風; 憶昔; seasonal wagashi.

Cash only; hot in summer; queues in the cherry-blossom and autumn seasons. Closed Wednesday.

One seasonal course built on outstanding dashi, around ¥100,000 a head. Regular service ends in March 2027 after a farewell year. Reservation by phone; jackets for men. Mon, Tue, Thu–Sat evenings.
places.chef: Hiroyuki Morikawa (森川裕之) · Third-generation owner (浜作三代目店主) and president of 株式会社浜作, per the official site · Gion, Kyoto (born 1962) · Per the official site: 森川裕之 was born in Gion-machi, Kyoto, in 1962, spent student days in Tokyo at kabuki, classical concerts and opera, and took over as third generation in 1991 on the death of the father, the second-generation 武; the founder, the grandfather 森川榮 (森川栄), opened Hamasaku on 1 September 1927 (Showa 2) in Gion Tominaga-cho as Japan’s first itamae kappo. The cookery school 浜作料理教室, started around the same time, has run some 2,300 sessions for 30,000 people; in 2017 the master was honoured as a Contemporary Master Craftsman, the youngest in Kyoto cuisine; books include 和食の教科書 ぎをん献立帖 and 京料理の品格. Guests listed on the site include the Showa Emperor, Kawabata Yasunari, Shiga Naoya, Mukoda Kuniko, Robert De Niro and Princess Grace of Monaco. The site announces that regular service ends at the end of March 2027, the 100th year, fulfilling a promise to the late father, after the master returned to the counter from a nine-hour heart operation over the New Year. Popular dishes sell out, so reserve them with the table, and book well ahead; 20:00 is easier at weekends. Smart casual. Closed Monday. A second shop has opened across the street.

Kitsune udon and rice bowls such as oyako-don are the alternatives. No bookings and no shared tables, so expect a queue — up to an hour or more in autumn 2026. Cash only; lunch daily, short evenings except Sundays.

places.notes: [Meat kaiseki · Gion, aged beef over charcoal] An 8-seat counter in a Gion alley where chef Yoshitaka Oka, a meat griller of over 20 years, cooks aged beef slowly over charcoal and firewood as a kaiseki course: Omi beef tartare laid out like a Kyoto garden, the Chateaubriand 'Oka katsu', and aged steaks from several farms, between soups and seasonal small dishes. Dinner runs about ¥30,000–50,000 a head plus 10% service. Reservation only; closed Tuesday. Aged meat has a distinct aroma — one regular warns it isn't for everyone.

A July 2025 reviewer says the restaurant was originally based in Shiga before moving to Kyoto; a March 2025 regular had visited before the relocation. Venison tripe, bear pâté, pheasant over charcoal, wild-boar spring rolls and botan-nabe come with Miyama's wild vegetables and house bread; reviewers say the meat has little gamey taste. Allow three hours — one December 2025 diner found service slow and the room cold. Reservation only; closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Kyoto Station, Kyoto–French in an old townhouse] A reservation-only kaiseki in a 100-year-old townhouse across the moat from Higashi Hongan-ji, five minutes from Kyoto Station. Chef Shohei Noguchi, from Fukushima and trained in France and at a sushi shop, mixes dashi, charcoal and rice with French sauces and organic vegetables: corn blancmange with sea urchin, Miwa somen dressed like pasta, ayu kamameshi to finish. Courses start together at 12:00 and 18:00; sit at the 9 m counter or in a private room. Dinner runs about ¥20,000–45,000; one October 2026 diner found it poor value.
places.chef: Shohei Noguchi · Head chef (Tabelog, shop text) · Fukushima Prefecture (September 2026 review) · Per a September 2026 reviewer: head chef Shohei Noguchi is from Fukushima; after culinary school the chef went to France in 2010 to train at a Michelin-starred restaurant, then worked at a Michelin-starred French restaurant in Osaka and trained in sushi at "Fuku Sushi Mori". A June 2026 reviewer says the shop received a Michelin star in 2019 under a different chef and that the current chef was born in 1990, with a young team aged 20s to 30s. Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): organic seasonings such as soy sauce, salt and mirin, and gratitude to producers, fishermen and farmers. · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): "To Producers, Fishermen, and Farmers: Elevating Gratitude for the Life of Food into Culinary Art." · Seasonal salad; Kyoto–French kaiseki.

places.notes: [French · Pontocho, French with chopsticks above the Kamo River] A long-running Pontocho French restaurant where a chef of more than twenty years in French cooking hides soy sauce in the sauces, serves the beef fillet with fresh wasabi and lays chopsticks on the table. From May to September you can eat on the yuka over the Kamo River at dusk. Courses only: a sea bream meunière or beef fillet at the centre, from ¥4,400 at lunch and ¥6,600 at dinner (more on the yuka). Book by phone; two-hour seating; cash only at lunch; closed Tuesday.

places.notes: [Mizutaki · Gion Nawate, seventy years of white chicken broth] A Gion house that has served one thing since 1955: mizutaki, Tanba chicken in a milky chicken-bone broth simmered for a day with well water from under the shop, dipped in house ponzu and finished as zosui. The ¥11,000 course starts with simmered liver and salt-grilled thigh. It reopened on 1 March 2026 after a long closure, with fewer seats — book ahead. Tatami rooms upstairs have tables and chairs. Closed Monday and Thursday.

places.notes: [Beef · Kyoto City Hall, raw tongue and heart in a machiya] A renovated machiya in a lane near City Hall, opened in 2019 by a chef who for many years led the kitchen at Anzan, the old Gion meat restaurant, and runs it with the chef’s daughter. Beef arrives in small plates in menu order — raw tongue, raw heart and yukhoe (¥1,200 each), blanched mino — until a Yanagawa-style dish signals the break; then order freely from the grill: tongue, tripe, loin, tail soup. About ten seats; reservations only, and the phone is busy. Closed Wednesday.

Many dishes come in half portions for solo diners. In the morning it turns into a reserved breakfast (¥2,400) of nine small dishes, rice and a vast block of tofu in vegetable broth. Opened 2025.

places.cu: Kyoto yoshoku since 1978, world-famous for the master’s "Happy Omurice" performance (official site; Tabelog) · omurice — a soft omelette slit open over ketchup chicken rice and finished with house demi-glace at the counter — ¥2,700 (March 2021), ¥3,000 (January–February 2026) · soup of the day (corn), cream croquette, chicken poêlé · sake, shochu, wine, cocktails (2024–2026 reviews; Tabelog)
places.notes: [Yoshoku · Kiyamachi-Sanjo, the omurice show] A 16-seat counter yoshoku down an alley near Pontocho, open since 1978, made world-famous by its master's 'Happy Omurice' — the omelette flipped, slit and spread over ketchup rice with a flourish, demi-glace on top, and the room singing along. Omurice ¥3,000 (2026); soup and cream croquettes too. Booking online only, and slots go within minutes; one-hour sittings, mostly overseas guests. One February 2026 diner found ¥3,000 a lot unless you count the show. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Motokichi Yukimura (幸村元吉) · Master (マスター), per the official site · The official site names the master as 幸村 元吉 (Motokichi Yukimura) and is titled "オムライスで世界をHappyに!" ("making the world Happy with omurice"), with a fan club, music and overseas omurice events listed in its news. Tabelog: born in Kyoto in 1978 (opening day 2 December 1978), a western-style restaurant pursuing its own style, built on the idea that being able to order what you want, when you want, in the amount you want is the gateway to deliciousness. Reviewers describe videos viewed more than 100 million times, a visit by the King of Malaysia (January 2025) and fame in Taiwan (October 2024). · Per Tabelog: "May the feelings of both the cooks and the diners be in perfect harmony." · Happy Omurice.

places.notes: [Sushi · Gion-Higashiyama, Hokkaido fish on red-vinegar rice] An eight-seat counter, opened March 2024 as the Kyoto sister of Sapporo's hard-to-book Sushi no Kura: a single omakase of about seven Hokkaido-led small dishes — herring roe with cream cheese, hairy-crab cream — then ten or so nigiri on mild red-vinegar rice, hand rolls and fish-bone miso soup, for ¥22,000–24,000. The chef speaks English to overseas guests. No changes to the course; reservation only. Tue–Sun evenings.
places.chef: Head chef (named only in a machine-translated review) · Reviewers in 2026 describe the shop as a sister of the Sapporo restaurant Sushi no Kura, produced by its chef, with Hokkaido ingredients, red-vinegar rice in Kyoto against rice vinegar in Sapporo (May 2026), and a friendly head chef who speaks English with overseas guests (August 2025; September 2026). A September 2026 review names the producer and the chef at the counter, but only in English translation, so the names are not used here. Tabelog gives the opening day as 26 March 2024. · Omakase of Hokkaido fish; smoked nodoguro nigiri.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · south of the Imperial Palace, one chef, eight seats] An eight-seat kaiseki counter near the Imperial Palace where the chef, trained at Wakuden and Gion Maruyama and once head chef at the inn Hiiragiya, cooks and serves alone, never giving a returning guest the same menu: crab in Tosa-vinegar jelly, karasumi mochi, a seasonal soup, hot pot, kamadaki rice. Omakase ¥23,100; Michelin one star (Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2025). No gluten-free; no fish or shellfish allergies. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 岩崎義則 · Owner-chef (店主), per the official site · Per the official site: drawn to cooking by an elder brother who was a cook, the owner trained at the Kyoto ryotei 和久傳 and 祇園丸山 and served as head chef at the inn 京の宿 柊家, then opened 御所 岩さき near the Imperial Palace in 2007 (Heisei 19); following the inn custom of changing the menu for guests staying several nights, the chef never serves the same menu twice; one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2025. A 2025 review says the restaurant moved from near Karasuma Oike and reopened here in 2021; reviewers in 2024–2026 note the chef runs everything alone. · Per the official site: "旬に寄り添い、心を満たす" — staying close to the season to satisfy the heart; a once-in-a-lifetime menu each visit. · Seasonal kaiseki omakase; kamadaki rice.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: the restaurant says it cannot accommodate gluten-free diets and asks such guests not to come (Tabelog).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a dashi-based kaiseki of fish, crab, shellfish, duck or beef hot pot; the restaurant cannot accommodate fish, shellfish or mollusc allergies (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Sichuan · Fuyacho, a new hidden Sichuan kitchen] A 19-seat Sichuan restaurant at the far end of the ground floor of a multi-tenant building on Fuyacho-dori, opened in January 2026 by chef Keiichi Hara, who trained at well-known restaurants and in China per an opening-day reviewer. Order à la carte: a six-item appetizer plate, mapo tofu, a celery-and-bitter-melon chili shrimp, black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork on the bone and crab fried rice, with Shaoxing-wine sodas — numbing and hot but refined, say reviewers; solo diners are offered half portions. Most spend ¥6,000–8,000. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Keiichi Hara · Chef (named in a January 2026 review); a September 2026 reviewer calls the chef the owner · Per a January 2026 opening-day reviewer: chef Keiichi Hara trained at renowned restaurants and in China before opening this Sichuan restaurant, which mixes traditional flavours with a modern sensibility. Another January 2026 reviewer came because a favourite chef had opened a shop and enjoyed this chef’s Sichuan cooking again after a long time. A September 2026 diner found three people running the room and an open kitchen. Opened 21 January 2026 (Tabelog). Name written only in Latin letters in the source. · Mapo tofu; Yuan-style chili shrimp; black-vinegar pork on the bone.
places.gfd: Ask. Sichuan dishes built on chili oil, bean pastes and sauces, with gyoza, buns, noodles and fried rice; no gluten information is published (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Mostly meat and seafood (mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, chili shrimp); a few vegetable plates such as steamed eggplant with leek and Sichuan pepper sauce and two Sichuan potato salads, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [French bistro · Karasuma, a late-night wine bistro] A two-floor bistro behind a green door in an alley off Ayakoji, styled on Paris back streets, with a wooden counter round the kitchen downstairs and small tables upstairs. The menu sticks to bistro classics — steak frites, French onion gratin soup, pâté, crab croquettes — plus burrata with whatever fruit is in season, a torched-cheese Bolognese and Parmesan gnocchi, with wines picked by the sommelier. Reviewers like the late hours and the English-speaking staff; one solo diner was given a smaller pasta portion. Open until 1:30 (to 23:00 on Wednesday).
places.chef: Operator 株式会社ＧＭＩ (Gion; invoice T6130001067887), which also runs 焼肉マウム and 居酒屋 マウム; chef not named · Per the official site: Bistro Maumu does not chase trends and loves the unchanging scene of Paris bistros — steak frites, a daily pasta, honest food at the end of the day — with a resident sommelier choosing classic French and Italian bottles and New World wines. Opened 31 May 2024 (Tabelog). The invoice number belongs to 株式会社ＧＭＩ, whose head office is at the 焼肉マウム address in Gion (NTA corporate-number site; Tabelog). · Per the official site: "We make food that makes people happy" — a place to reset after work, not a special place you visit stiffly. · Steak frites; burrata with seasonal fruit; Parmesan-cream gnocchi.

The owner explains the coffee of the day; the blend (¥550) is Kenya-based and the soft, silky pudding (¥450) with bitter caramel is the reason most come — it must be ordered with a drink. Tabelog Cafe 'Tabelog 100' 2021 and WEST 2025. Small and quiet: no groups over five. Closed Wednesday and the third Sunday.

places.notes: [Korean · Pontocho, wagyu and kimchi over the Kamo River] The Kyoto branch of an Osaka-born chef's Korean restaurant that began in Daikanyama in 2000, here since 2009 and now in a stone-and-wood building on Pontocho with a counter round the kitchen and second-floor tables over the Kamo River. Courses open with a seasonal porridge and the house kimchi, then chijimi of Kyoto Kujo-negi, japchae and a main such as dakhanmari, bulgogi hot pot or black-pork samgyeopsal (¥7,000–12,000); à la carte runs to wagyu by the gram and bossam kimchi with seasonal fruit. 10% service. Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST 'Tabelog 100' 2026.
places.chef: 李 南河 · Owner-chef of the operator group (grate-ful.co.jp); the shop carries the chef’s own name · Osaka (official site). · Per the official site: in 2000 the Osaka-born cook 李 南河 opened 代官山 李南河 in Tokyo, naming it after the chef in the hope that guests feel as if eating at home; the Kyoto sister shop opened in a renovated old house in a Pontocho back alley and later moved to the riverside within Pontocho; the owner-chef visits producers and markets and buys wagyu at the Kyoto meat market; selected by ZAGAT and as a best Korean restaurant by the Korean Food Foundation; the bulgogi shop SURAGAN (Ebisu) followed in 2005. The operator グレイトフル株式会社 lists 9 restaurants and delis in Tokyo, Kanagawa and Kyoto, two named 李南河, and dates the Kyoto opening to July 2009 (grate-ful.co.jp). The invoice holder is the group company グレイトフルオペレーション株式会社 (Tabelog; NTA). · Per the official site: to keep trying new things with carefully chosen seasonal ingredients so people learn how good Korean food is. · Bossam kimchi with seasonal fruit; Kujo-negi chijimi; dakhanmari and bulgogi hot pots.

Omakase only: lunch ¥12,000, dinner ¥22,000, plus 10%. English menu and staff; no vegan or vegetarian meals. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
places.chef: 古賀 隆稚 (Koga Ryuji) · Chef · Fukuoka Prefecture (official site). · Per the official site: after École Tsuji's school in France and training in regional France, worked from 2006 at Joël Robuchon (Ebisu), then in France at Le Chabichou (Courchevel), Villa Archange (Cannes), Ledoyen (Paris) and as sous-chef at a one-star restaurant; from 2016 the first Japanese deputy head chef, also developing menus, at Le Cinq (Hôtel George V, Paris) under Christian Le Squer; back in Japan in 2019 as head chef at the Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto. RED U-35 bronze egg 2013 and silver egg 2014 and 2015. Opened KOGA on 9 January 2025 (Tabelog). places.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Gion Shirakawa, a counter by the stone lane] A tiny counter hidden on the Shirakawa stone lane in Gion, with eight seats in front of the cooks and one table. The nine-course omakase is ¥11,000, or order à la carte from the seasonal list: rolled omelette, karasumi with daikon, salt-grilled Kyoto chicken, saba-zushi to finish, and old-Kyoto drinking snacks such as funazushi and whale bacon. The head chef, named 筒井 on the official site, trained within the yagenbori group. ¥1,000 otoshi; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 筒井 (head chef; reading not given) · Head chef 筒井, promoted after training at yagenbori (official site), Operated by the yagenbori group · The official site says the head chef, 筒井, was chosen to lead Wabisuke after training at yagenbori, and that the kitchen blends Kyoto tradition with new arrangements. A March 2026 reviewer first came about 35 years ago, when an elderly woman ran it alone; it later joined the yagenbori group, and the chef has changed on each visit since. A February 2026 reviewer says the present head chef has led the kitchen for a few years. · To bring out the character of fish from around Kyoto and Kyoto vegetables in Kyoto cuisine that shows the four seasons (official site). · Seasonal omakase; karasumi with daikon; saba-zushi.

A sister of the soba shop next door, suba, so it works well before or after. Mostly standing; one November 2025 visitor found the system unexplained.

Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

places.notes: [Fish izakaya · Shimabara, the market’s back door] An unsigned izakaya in old Shimabara beside Kyoto’s Central Wholesale Market, where the cooks work at a counter level with your plate and the fish comes from a trusted market wholesaler. Evenings are courses — ¥6,000 or ¥9,900 — that change completely between visits: rare sashimi such as akou and ojisan, shio-koji yellowtail, simmered kinmedai head, cod fry, omakase sushi. Lunch has stopped for now. Closed Sunday and holidays; junior-high age and up.

places.cu: “Everyday Kyoto cuisine”: the original ochazuke house, a light meal of rice, pickles and sides (official site) · Suzushiro set ¥1,500 — dashimaki, red-miso soup, rice in a wooden tub for about two bowls, assorted seasonal pickles, hojicha (official site; July–September 2026) · Mizuna set with a seasonal simmered dish; a set with sea bream nanban (2026 reviews) · dashimaki of two eggs and a strong…
places.notes: [Ochazuke · Marutamachi, Kyoto’s everyday meal since the Taisho era] An old machiya by the Imperial Palace serving “ochazuke” in the Kyoto sense — a modest meal. The Suzushiro set (¥1,500, lunch or dinner) brings a feather-light rolled omelette made with a dashi started at 4 a.m., red-miso soup, a tub of rice and seasonal pickles, with Ippodo hojicha for the ochazuke. No reservations and queues in autumn; dinner ends early, at 19:00. Staff greet in soft Kyoto dialect and speak English. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Family business (unnamed in the sources) · Per the official site: an ochazuke house in business since the Taisho era. It began as a sweets shop in Gion named Junidanya after the twelve acts of Chushingura; ochazuke served to settle the palates of tipsy customers proved so popular that it has continued ever since. The site lists TV and press coverage and a 2025 article recalling 長嶋茂雄 as a patron. · Ochazuke as Kyoto cuisine in everyday dress — plain food that cannot hide anything; local and contract-farm vegetables, Ippodo tea (official site). · Dashimaki; the Suzushiro ochazuke set.

places.notes: [Sandwiches · downtown, Brooklyn katsu sando with sake] A twelve-seat counter south of Sanjo, the Kyoto outpost of a Brooklyn sando shop ("HELLO, Kyoto! WE ARE FROM BROOKLYN"), with a second Kyoto shop at Kiyomizu. Freshly fried pork or chicken katsu with cabbage and house sauce on milk bread, ¥1,500; egg-salad sando ¥1,300; beef fillet katsu ¥4,000. Portions are big — several diners took half home — and one found the sauce about to spill out. Sake picked by the owner-sommelier. English menu and staff; many overseas customers. Daily 12:00–17:00.
places.chef: Sakaki Nakamura (owner and sommelier, per the Sanjo menu; name known only in Latin letters) · Owner and sake sommelier (Sanjo menu: "Sakaki Nakamura, the owner/sommelier, curates fine sake from all over Japan") · Taku Sando began in Greenpoint, Brooklyn (29 Greenpoint Ave), "brought to you by the creative team of Takumen in LIC", around a shokupan milk bread baked in-house daily (takusando.com About page). The Kyoto site lists two Kyoto shops, Sanjo and Kiyomizu, beside Brooklyn; the Sanjo menu is headed "HELLO, Kyoto! WE ARE FROM BROOKLYN." The Sanjo shop opened on 15 October 2024 (Tabelog). · From the Brooklyn About page: the shokupan "represents a wholesome luxury, and is the heart of the meal". · Pork katsu sando; chicken katsu sando; tamago sando.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: every sandwich is on house shokupan milk bread, and the katsu and croquettes are coated in panko (Sanjo menu).

places.notes: [Takoyaki · Gion, until 4 am] A thirteen-seat L-shaped counter under red lanterns on the ground floor of a club building on Hanamikoji, frying takoyaki till 4 am; diners say it has been there 20 years, with a second-generation owner greeting passers-by. Eight crisp-shelled, gooey balls for ¥800 in seventeen flavours — sauce, salt, pizza, seaweed kimchi — plus half-and-half; champagne and sake beside the beer. One diner found the beer glass small; another felt chilly in the half-open room in autumn and a little intimidated by the street at night. Smoking allowed. Cash or e-money.
places.chef: Second-generation owner (January 2026 review); not named in a source · The shop blog (ameblo, last updated 2012) calls 秀蛸 a takoyaki shop born in Kyoto, with a Gion main shop and a Kiyamachi shop; a February 2012 post mentions staff from all three shops of the time. Tabelog lists the Gion shop and a Kiyamachi shop today. A June 2025 diner and a January 2026 diner say it has been running for 20 years; the January 2026 diner calls the energetic young owner the second generation. · Takoyaki in many sauces, with half-and-half plates.

places.notes: [Italian & shaved ice · Gion south, Matayoshi's casual sister] The casual sister of Gion Matayoshi, also on the south side of Gion, behind a patterned block lattice: by day a fish or wagyu lunch tray and natural-ice kakigori with house syrups, by night Italian à la carte on kaiseki plates — sea-urchin aglio e olio, wagyu Bolognese, veal cutlet. Diners in 2025–2026 praised sea-bream chazuke, rich matcha ice and warm send-offs; others found a ¥1,800 matcha ice average (July 2026), slow drinks with two staff (July 2026), and food average with uneven pacing and few drinks (October 2026). No cash.

The また吉 site itself says it was born in October 2026, serving Italian with the same chosen ingredients and preparation as the main restaurant plus natural-ice shaved ice at casual prices; an August 2026 diner mentions a recent renovation, and an October 2026 diner calls it still new. A July 2026 diner writes that the owner hails from Okinawa. places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion south, ten seats and handmade soba] A ten-seat kaiseki counter east of Hanamikoji, opened in 2014 and starred in the 2016 Michelin Guide (Tabelog). Courses start with a brown-rice soup and freshly shaved bonito, run through hamo, sweetfish and eel, and end with the owner’s own 100% buckwheat soba. An April 2026 couple found it rare for Gion: lightly seasoned, traditional Kyoto cooking from ¥12,000 at night, with the owners seeing them off. The site says no English is spoken — book through your hotel. Cash only. Closed Thursday.
places.chef: Moriwaki (surname from the shop name; Tabelog gives a full name only in machine translation, so it is not used) · Owner-chef (店主), per the official site · Per the official site: a small ten-seat shop born in Gion in 2014, serving seasonal kaiseki that ends with the owner’s handmade 100% buckwheat soba. Tabelog (in its English translation): the chef trained at ryokans, sushi restaurants and other places, then at "Irifune" and "Gion Okada" before going independent; opened 28 August 2014; a Michelin star in the 2016 Michelin Guide, about a year after opening. A January 2025 diner was served by the head chef, the proprietress and another chef. · Official site: to be a shop that always stays close by, for time alone or time with someone dear. · Seasonal kaiseki; handmade 100% buckwheat soba to finish.

places.notes: [Tempura · Gion, a six-seat counter] A tiny tempura counter on a Gion corner, where one chef fries course after course in front of six guests. Dinner (¥7,700 or ¥12,100) starts with wagyu tail soup, sashimi and seared wagyu, then about ten seasonal pieces — kuruma prawn, aosa seaweed piled with sea urchin, Kamo eggplant, eel, young ayu in summer, a rare-fried wagyu — and ends with a tempura rice ball. Lunch from ¥3,300 is the value pick. Book by the day before. Run by the small Kyoto group 京色; reviewers like the quiet chef and the price for Gion.
places.chef: Head chef (not named) who runs the counter alone (June 2026); operator 株式会社京色 · Per the operator site: 株式会社京色 was founded by its president 眞鍋 and the cooks 藤原 and 山内, who studied together at a cooking school and gained experience in Japanese, Western and creative cooking before reuniting; the company runs 5 Kyoto shops — うらやま京色, BANSAN 京色, 祇園 晩餐 京色, 祇園天ぷら晩餐 and 角打ちと麺 ばんさん. The chef told a July 2026 diner the oil is 100% cottonseed. · Per the official page: tempura needs both fresh ingredients and the cook’s skill — no letting up from buying to the moment it is served. · Aosa tempura topped with sea urchin; wagyu tail soup; tempura rice ball.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Gion, Niigata sake till 3 a.m.] A small, smoky, late-night izakaya on Gion's Kiritoshi, run by an owner from Niigata. It pours Niigata sake — ask for the off-menu bottles — with a long list of homey plates: tuna macaroni salad, nikujaga, horse sashimi, giant Tochio fried tofu with negi miso, oden in winter, and the namesake pork miso soup to finish. Mostly locals, Showa pop on the speakers, ¥500 cover. Open until 3:00; closed Sunday.

Reviewers describe an owner from Niigata (June and October 2025) and a master who sometimes drinks along with guests (April 2025). Opened 26 November 2013 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: "空間、人、美味しさ" — the space, the people and good food; at-home and hidden at once. · Pork miso soup; Tochio fried tofu with negi miso; Niigata sake.

places.cu: Wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki cooked at the table by staff in the house warishita (official site) · dinner: wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki ¥24,500, Omi-beef sukiyaki ¥30,500, Omi-beef shabu-shabu with kombu dashi, house ponzu and sesame sauce ¥30,500 (book ahead), Kobe-beef sukiyaki ¥36,500, Omi-beef chateaubriand sukiyaki (limited) ¥42,500 — each with a starter, soup, the main, rice and dessert · weekend lunch…
places.notes: [Sukiyaki · Kiyamachi, private rooms over the Kamo River] A sukiyaki house in private rooms down a stone alley off Kiyamachi, in the building where the Bakumatsu samurai Takechi Hanpeita lodged when it was the ryotei 四国屋丹虎; some rooms look over the Kamo River, one onto a tsukubai garden by Kazuyuki Ishihara. Staff cook wagyu, Omi or Kobe beef sukiyaki at the table in the house warishita, after seasonal kaiseki starters; dinner from ¥24,500, weekend lunch from ¥12,100, service included. Reviewers praise the rooms and the river terrace; one found the sukiyaki too light. Run by the Kobe-based G LION GROUP. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 料理長 (head chef, not named); operator G LION GROUP (Kobe; representative 菊地 秀武) · Per the official site: wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki in a new style by a cook long experienced in traditional Japanese cuisine, made in front of guests with the house warishita; the building was the ryotei 四国屋丹虎 in the Bakumatsu era, where 武市半平太 lived when in Kyoto, and the tokonoma board and pillar of the 半平の間 are kept unchanged; a box-staircase trace from that era was found during renovation; tsubo-niwa garden supervised by the garden designer 石原和幸. Press releases name the operator as the G LION GROUP of Kobe (representative 菊地 秀武), whose recruitment site describes about 150 group companies, mostly car dealerships. places.notes: [Izakaya · Sanbongi, charcoal and natural wine in an old townhouse] A hard-to-book izakaya in a century-old townhouse near the Kamo River, with a nine-seat counter and one big shared table. The idea is charcoal and drink: binchotan-grilled boar, venison, duck and pasture pork, plus a long handwritten list of inventive small plates — lemongrass clams, ayu-and-basil spring rolls, tuna tartare — with natural wine from the cellar and warm sake. Book by phone once the calendar is out on Instagram; an August 2026 reviewer says non-drinkers are not admitted. About ¥8,000–15,000 a head. Tabelog izakaya WEST 'Tabelog 100' 2026.
places.chef: Not named in any source found; an October 2026 reviewer says the staff moved here from Tokyo · Per the official site: an izakaya built on charcoal grilling with wine and sake — vin nature that reflects the land without chemical help, sake mainly served warm — and ingredients raised with passion by the producers, grilled over binchotan; in a renovated Kyoto townhouse more than 100 years old in Sanbongi, once a lively pleasure quarter. Opened 28 March 2019 (Tabelog). Tabelog izakaya WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026 (Tabelog). An August 2026 reviewer says the place was started as a sophisticated bar for wine and sake with good food. · Per the official site: wines that reflect the land of origin, sake served warm, and producers’ ingredients grilled over binchotan. · Binchotan-grilled game and duck; natural wine.

places.notes: [Kappo izakaya · Gion off Hanamikoji, 50 years upstairs] A long-running Gion izakaya on the fifth floor of an old Showa building, reached by a narrow alley off Hanamikoji, serving seasonal fish and Kyoto home cooking from a daily list of fifty-plus dishes: hamo, duck aburi, grilled eel and sweetfish, dobin-mushi in autumn, with local sake. Prices are fair for Gion, but the menu shows none, which unsettled some visitors; one June 2025 guest was put off by the chef correcting staff in front of diners. A ¥770 otoshi. Closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Takatsuji Takakura, Kitcho-trained, Shugakuin vegetables] A ten-seat counter south of Bukko-ji where owner-chef 八木一真, after 16 years at Arashiyama Kitcho and 8 at Hiiragiya, cooks monthly kaiseki around vegetables grown for the shop at a 300-year-old farm inside the Shugakuin Imperial Villa. Sashimi with the house plum sauce and wasabi, a themed hassun, donabe rice and homemade sweets are the talk of reviews. Lunch ¥11,000–15,000 (Wed, Fri, Sun), dinner ¥22,000–26,000, plus 10% service. Book at least two days ahead; give notice of allergies then. Closed Monday.
places.chef: 八木一真 (romaji not given in the sources) · Owner-chef, Service staff · Per the official site: the owner, 八木一真, decided to become a cook as a student on discovering the joy of being told the food was delicious, trained for 16 years at Kyoto Arashiyama Kitcho and 8 years at Hiiragiya ryokan, and opened Kanzan; the shop marked its 10th anniversary on 10 November 2026. A July 2023 reviewer says the head chef comes from a family of pottery craftsmen. Reviewers describe the chef with a service staff member (January 2026) and the chef and the owner running the place together (May 2026). places.notes: [Soup house · Kawaramachi, since 1932] A soup house down a lane off Kawaramachi, open since 1932, with a counter built like a Noh stage and seats styled on the railings of the Sanjo and Gojo bridges. The draw is the Rikyu bento (¥3,300): five small dishes, kayaku rice and a bowl of sweet white-miso soup — swap the tofu for grated yam or sweet potato. Light, gentle flavours; small portions. Cash only; queues before opening on holidays. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Head chef and cooks (unnamed) · Per the official site: founded in Showa 7 (1932); the name comes from 汁講, a frugal custom in which guests brought rice and the host provided only soup, said to descend from a Heian-period practice; the interior keeps the founder's touches — a counter modelled on a Noh stage and seats styled after the railings of the Sanjo and Gojo bridges. A September 2026 reviewer saw artisans and the head chef bustling about. · "The spirit of hospitality put into a single cup of soup" (official site). · Rikyu bento; white-miso soup.

places.notes: [Wagyu kappo · near Kyoto Station, an 1890 townhouse] A twelve-seat counter in an 1890 Kyoto townhouse at the end of a quiet stone alley, eight minutes from Kyoto Station, that serves Kyoto black wagyu as a kappo course: seared with ponzu jelly, as tataki and sashimi, in a strip-loin rice bowl, a tenderloin sandwich, shabu-shabu soup and tempura. Courses about ¥20,000–22,000 plus 10% service; two-hour seatings. Open daily, lunch and dinner.

places.notes: [Kappo · Gion, fish and wild game] A Gion kappo, renovated in 2026, where the chef cooks seasonal fish alongside rare game — wild boar, badger, bear hot pot, even sea turtle in a special course — as an omakase or from a handwritten à la carte list. Sake is chosen by a sake sommelier; finish with takikomi gohan or a mini tantanmen and take home a katsu sandwich. The counter gets loud with a lively chef and regulars, and the upstairs bar louder later. Omakase from ¥20,000 plus tax and 10% service. Evenings only.

One monthly course of about ten dishes for ¥22,000 — a cold capellini in shark broth with caviar, squid-ink tagliolini, a risotto, Hiroshima beef — with the championship tonnarelli as an extra. Most diners are delighted; one August 2026 diner found it rushed and overpriced. Plus 5% service. Book well ahead; closed Sunday.

The handwritten menu is home cooking with a twist: potato salads in changing flavours, kitsune cheese, breaded swordfish, anchovy cabbage, an egg sandwich, keema curry. Two burners only, so be patient when it is full. No cards (QR is fine); smoking allowed; closed Sunday.

places.notes: [French bistro · Pontocho Kaburenjo, Sasue fish in Kyoto] A relaxed French-and-yoshoku restaurant next to the Pontocho Kaburenjo whose draw is fish from Sasue Maeda, the celebrated fishmonger of Yaizu, alongside vegetables from the chef’s family farm. Lunch runs from a ¥2,900 omurice set to five-course menus; dinner courses go to about ¥10,000, with fish burgers, puff-pastry snapper, wagyu over whisky-barrel wood and a curry to close. A vegan menu is offered. ¥200 charge; English spoken; closed Monday.

Spacious and calm, popular for birthdays with family. Book by phone; closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Kappo · Okazaki, a counter in sight of the Heian Shrine torii] Upstairs on Jingu-michi, a twelve-seat counter run by a chef who trained at Tankuma, then spent more than a decade at Inaba and Gion Ima, and opened here in 2024 with the chef’s wife at front of house. Order a course (¥15,000 or ¥20,000) or graze à la carte from the board in small portions: hamo and ayu in summer, seko-gani in winter, whale bacon, a soft-shelled-turtle porridge to finish. Warm, chatty hosts. Closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Miyagawacho, a playful Kyoto counter] An eight-seat counter on Miyagawacho's stone-paved lane of teahouses, run by a chef-sommelier who trained at Gion Sasaki. The omakase (about ¥26,400–28,600) moves from classic Kyoto dishes — fugu broth over grilled fins, house karasumi on rice, hamo and ayu in summer — to playful turns such as fugu milt with truffle, a mini seafood ramen and the signature fillet beef cutlet sandwich, before donabe rice. Diners in May 2026 found the entrance full of flowers for a new Michelin star. Everyone starts together; book ahead. Closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Italian · Philosopher's Path, wood-fired vegetables and pizza] A fourteen-seat restaurant in a house on the Philosopher's Path, where chef 今井 義浩 (Imai) cooks nearly everything in a wood-fired oven: a plain dough 'suyaki' pizza to start, then vegetables picked up each morning from Ohara farms, fish and seasonal plates, and a closing half-and-half pizza such as shirasu or venison ragù with sansho. One course, about ¥15,400; counter seats face the fire. Featured on Netflix's Chef's Table, it is booked months ahead, mostly by overseas guests. Closed Monday.
places.chef: 今井 義浩 · Owner-chef (pizza maker) · Per the restaurant’s own text (on yousakana.jp): a small restaurant on the Philosopher’s Path cooking simple food over live fire, with pizza from the wood-fired oven as the main dish; every morning the chef visits farms in the mountains of Ohara and markets around Kyoto. Tabelog notes the owner-chef paused in January 2020 to focus on writing and reopened in March 2020. Reviewers note the opening in December 2015, training at renowned restaurants abroad including one in Denmark and in California (October 2023), and a Netflix Chef’s Table episode (2024). places.notes: [Italian · Kyoto Station, hotel Italian up the grand staircase] The Italian restaurant of THE THOUSAND KYOTO, two minutes from Kyoto Station, reached up the hotel's grand staircase. Chef Kenta Shibahara, born in Kyoto and trained at a Michelin-starred restaurant in Naples, cooks seasonal courses that play with texture — corn 'carbonara', Kamo eggplant spaghettini with white miso — paired by a sommelier team known for competition results. Lunch courses are the easy way in; 15% service on top. 110 seats and private rooms; closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 芝原 健太 (Kenta Shibahara) · 料理長 (head chef) of SCALAE; operator 京阪ホテルズ＆リゾーツ株式会社 · Kyoto (press release). · Per the hotel’s September 2026 press release: 芝原 健太, born in Kyoto, went to Italy in 2009 and learned European technique at a Michelin-starred ristorante in Naples, then became SCALAE’s chef at THE THOUSAND KYOTO in 2021, building the cooking on “素材自然回帰” — conveying each producer’s thoughts and philosophy to the diner. The hotel is the Keihan group’s flagship; the invoice number belongs to 京阪ホテルズ＆リゾーツ株式会社 (NTA corporate-number site). Its sommelier team is led by the beverage director 岩田 渉 (A.S.I. World’s Best Sommelier semi-finalist, fifth in 2023) and chef-sommelier 沖中 亮真 (press release). Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 (Tabelog). · Per the press release: "素材自然回帰" — a return to the ingredient and its producer, seeking flavour rooted in harmony. · Seasonal Italian courses with wine or tea pairings.

places.notes: [Soba · Higashinotoin, a 1916 soba house reborn] A soba and udon house founded in 1916, long in Pontocho and later in Daimaru, that closed at the end of 2024 and reopened in December 2025 in a new wooden shop near Shijo — with the old head chef, cookware and signboard, after a crowdfunding drive. Tempura zaru, nishin, kitsune, okame and seasonal bowls run about ¥1,400–1,900; some find it a little dear. English menu; cards and QR. Open 11:00–19:00. Closed Monday.

Regulars rank its mackerel sushi above the famous names. One March 2026 diner waited 30 minutes and found it nothing special. Take-away by phone. Closed Monday and Tuesday.

Seasonal Kyoto kaiseki from ¥8,800 at lunch and ¥12,100 at dinner, its grilled course centred on charcoal-grilled Omi Hime wagyu (or fish if you prefer), plus an anago rice box lunch from ¥2,530. Reviewers find it classic rather than surprising, and good for entertaining. 10% service (more in private rooms).

places.notes: [Italian · Nijo, a Piedmontese ristorante with Kyoto vegetables] A white house near Nijo Station where chef Watanabe — a Piedmont wine lover who goes to the harvest there each year — has cooked northern Italian food with Kyoto and organic vegetables since 1999. Start with the showpiece platter of seasonal vegetables and house hams, then handmade pasta such as egg-yolk tajarin or cold fedelini with sea urchin, with Piedmontese wine; white truffle, porcini and white asparagus arrive in season. Gluten-free rice- or corn-flour pasta is offered. Lunch courses from about ¥5,500; ¥300 table charge at dinner.
places.chef: 渡辺 (Watanabe) · Owner-chef of the Il Viale group (株式会社イルヴィアーレ); given name not published · Per the group site: chef Watanabe first went to Italy at 21 to see Ferraris and Ducatis, was won over by the food, trained at well-known Italian restaurants in Kyoto and Tokyo, worked for a time on a farm in Kamigamo, and opened Cucina Il Viale at Horikawa-Oike in 1999; Kyoto-vegetable pasta met resistance at first ("put some bacon in it"), but ten years of keeping to it led to running five shops — Ca’ del Viale, TAVERNA il Viale, the gluten-free deli AL CAMINO, PANINOTECA and LA RISOTTERIA in the Daimaru Kyoto store; the chef goes to Piedmont every year to help with the grape harvest. The invoice number belongs to 株式会社イルヴィアーレ (NTA). Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 (Tabelog). A March 2025 reviewer found the chef cooking at the counter with an assistant. · Per the group site: "本当に美味しいものはいつか認められる" — truly good food is recognised in time. · Antipasto of Kyoto vegetables and house hams; handmade tajarin; Piedmont wine.
places.gfd: Some GF options: the official menu says gluten-free pasta made from rice flour or corn flour is available, and the group runs a gluten-free deli (AL CAMINO). places.notes: [Chinese · Shijo-Karasuma, Hong Kong dim sum from the carts] A big Hong Kong-style Cantonese restaurant in the basement of COCON KARASUMA, run since 2004 by a Kobe-born group whose cooks are from Hong Kong and Guangdong. The draw is the dim sum course: for ¥5,000 eight carts roll round with about sixty kinds of dim sum, congee, noodles and desserts for 90 minutes. Evenings bring shark fin, abalone, live-tank seafood, Peking duck and Shanghai crab in season. A longtime regular complains prices have doubled in two years. 10% service; open daily.
places.chef: 陳 李富 · 総料理長 (head chef) since 2026; with 料理相談役 劉 錦超 and general manager 陳 暁冬; operator KDA株式会社 · Guangdong (official site). · Per the official site: the restaurant began in Kobe’s Ijinkan district and opened in Kyoto with COCON KARASUMA in December 2004, operated by KDA株式会社. Head chef 陳 李富 (born 1964 in Guangdong) cooked Hong Kong food for ten years from 1982, joined 老香港酒家 after coming to Japan in 1992, became sous-chef in 2018 and head chef in 2026; culinary adviser 劉 錦超 (born 1965 in Taishan, Guangdong) joined in 2004, was head chef from 2018 and specialises in dried shark fin, abalone and shiitake, and Buddha-jumps-over-the-wall soup; general manager 陳 暁冬 (born 1972 in Beijing) says eight dim sum carts run 365 days a year and nine cooks visit Hong Kong regularly to research. Tabelog Chinese WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023 and 2024 (Tabelog). · Per the general manager on the official site: "没有最好 只有更好" — there is no best, only better. · Dim sum from the carts; shark fin and abalone; live-tank seafood.

places.chef: 野澤 孝彦 (のざわ・たかひこ, per the official site) · Chef of the Japanese shop, entrusted with the recipes by Robert Edegger (official site) · Born 1972 in 埼玉県上尾市 (official site). · Per the official site: Hofbäckerei Edegger-Tax in Graz, founded in 1569, held the Habsburg court warrant; the eighth-generation owner Robert Edegger, in charge since 1992, entrusted the recipes to 野澤 孝彦 and opened the Japanese shop, "from Graz to Kyoto". 野澤 was drawn to Austrian culture through piano lessons, went to Vienna at 22 and trained at the café houses Oberlaa and L. Heiner, learned bread-making at Wandinger in southern Germany, opened Neues in Japan in 1999 and received the recipes from Robert Edegger in 2012. A September 2026 diner remembers the shop near Mansei-bashi in Tokyo and writes that it has moved twice. Firm, cold zaru soba (¥800), a huge kakiage soba, duck or herring soba, and a beef sukiyaki with soba or udon, to jazz in the background. Few tourists find it, though a queue can form. Closed Wednesday and every other Thursday.

places.notes: [Kappo · Marutamachi, the angler chef's ayu] A small kappo near the Imperial Palace, formerly on Kawaramachi, where the owner — a keen angler who fishes for ayu on the weekly day off — cooks seasonal Kyoto dishes with the chef’s wife serving. Summer is the time: live ayu as sashimi and double-grilled until you can eat it bones and all, a side-by-side of wild and Lake Biwa ayu, and ayu rice to finish; spring brings young ayu and pea rice, autumn matsutake. Hard to book without an introduction; about ¥15,000–30,000. Closed Monday per regulars.

places.notes: [Chinese · Higashiyama, 25 small dishes in an old townhouse] A modern Chinese restaurant in an old Kyoto townhouse south of Yasaka Shrine, opened in November 2024. Michelin-listed. 10% service; a ¥3,000 water charge if you order no drinks. Two dinner seatings.

Every course centres on refillable oboro yudofu, with dengaku, yuba and soy-milk dishes around it, from a ¥5,000 lunch. Unusually, there is a fully plant-based course, 六波羅 (no meat, fish, egg, dairy or fish dashi), and gluten-free versions of two courses — book these three days ahead. Open daily.
places.chef: Head chef (unnamed), per the official site · Per the official site: 豆水楼 has two shops, on Kiyamachi (a Taisho-era townhouse on the Kamo River, with a summer yuka) and in Gion (a machiya with a storehouse room, 古蔵庵). The site says gluten-free courses were started in response to many requests, mostly from visitors from abroad. The speciality is andouillette — the shop holds the AAAAA certification, the first outside France — alongside boudin noir, escargots, onion soup, steak and red-wine beef, with crêpes Suzette to finish and organic wines. Good value; book on Fridays. Closed Tuesday.

places.notes: [Kissaten · Kawaramachi, jelly punch under blue light since 1948] A two-floor coffee house by the Takase River, opened in 1948 and designed with artist friends of the founder: carved wood by the sculptor 池野禎春, blue lights chosen by a dye scholar, paintings by 東郷青児 and other Nika-kai artists, and no background music. Order the jelly punch (¥850) — five colours of jelly sparkling in soda, created by the second owner's wife in the 1970s — or a cream soda, with thick toast to share. Chairs are small; expect a queue at weekends. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Family-run since 1948 (founder 元木和夫; jelly menu by 元木成子, wife of the second owner); current owner not named · Per the official site: opened on 11 April 1948, just after the war; the building and furnishings were created by the founder 元木和夫’s cultural friends — painter 佐々木良三, sculptor 池野禎春 (whose French training shaped the carved interior), dye scholar 上村六郎 (who suggested the blue light that makes women look beautiful and men young) and count-poet 𠮷井勇 (whose poem stands by the door); the line drawings on the cups were drawn for the shop by 東郷青児; 元木成子 (1937–1991), wife of the second owner, created the jelly drinks — first jelly milk for a daughter who disliked milk, then jelly punch from 1975 to bring in young women. The shop sells original Koransha cups and holds the jelly punch trademark (official site). · Per the official site: "Soirée" means an evening party — a dreamlike room that feels like night even by day. · Jelly punch; cream soda.

Around it, Kyoto obanzai, grilled nama-fu, Tanba-beef or mochi-pork shabu-shabu and yuba-ankake rice, with plenty of Kyoto sake. Not cheap for the portions, some say. ¥390 seat charge; closed Wednesday.

Reviewers spot Okinawan touches such as sea grapes, goya and brown-sugar sorbet. Easy for solo diners; ¥800 otoshi if you skip the course.

Help yourself to free tenkasu and crunchy fried iriko. Buy a ticket, order, then grab a seat. Open daily.

places.cu: Takeaway Kyoto wagashi (Tabelog) · warabi mochi of authentic bracken starch with brown sugar, kinako of Tanba black soybeans and wasanbon, featured on Matsuko no Shiranai Sekai; small (serves two) ¥1,000, large (serves four) ¥2,000; keeps a week at room temperature (2025–2026 reviews) · monaka, tea monaka ¥200 (January 2026) · ohagi, sakura mochi (April 2025) · minazuki in season; mango and other…
places.notes: [Wagashi · Aburanokoji, the warabi mochi] A small machiya sweet shop near the Kyoto Prefectural Office, with no seats — you buy and take away. The draw is a soft, melting warabi mochi of real bracken starch and brown sugar under homemade kinako of Tanba black soybeans, ¥1,000 for a small pack that keeps a week; it was featured on Matsuko no Shiranai Sekai. Also monaka, ohagi and seasonal sweets. The owner trained at Kameya Kiyonaga in Gion. Cash only.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), trained at Kameya Kiyonaga in Gion · A February 2025 review, quoting the shop’s own introduction, says “The owner trained at the famous ‘Kameya Kiyonaga’ shop in Gion before establishing this place.” In December 2023 a reviewer described a shop “operated by an elderly couple” with the couple’s son; in January 2026 another described an elderly gentleman running the shop alone, hands covered in warabi mochi and kinako while packing. A July 2026 regular of four years noted the sweets now come pre-packed, where four years earlier each order was taken from the fridge, cut, weighed and packed on the spot, and that prices had gone up. · Warabi mochi with homemade kinako.
places.gfd: Ask. The warabi mochi is described as made from authentic bracken starch with brown sugar, dusted with kinako of Tanba black soybeans and wasanbon (2023–2026 reviews), but no ingredient list is published; the shop also sells monaka, ohagi, sakura mochi and daifuku, not described.
places.vgd: Ask. The warabi mochi as described is bracken starch, brown sugar, kinako and wasanbon (2023–2026 reviews), but no full ingredient list is published.

places.notes: [Patisserie · Shogoin, opposite the university hospital] A small, chic cake shop so understated that people walk past it, across from Kyoto University Hospital. Open four days a week from noon until sold out; check Instagram. Reviewers call it refined; a few find it heavy or sweet.

places.chef: 和久 秀郎 (Waku Hiderō) · Owner-chef · Itami, Hyogo (official site) · Per his own profile page: born 12 February 1982 in Itami, Hyogo; 174 cm, blood type O. Studied at 育成調理師専門学校 in Hyogo, a three-year cooking school combined with high school, 1997–2000, working part-time in an izakaya, an udon chain and a family restaurant; cook’s licence 2000. From April 2000 worked at ryotei in Kyoto — one with a Kamo River summer platform, one at Nanzenji, one in Nishikyo — then filled in at dozens of kitchens: a sushi kappo in Shinsaibashi, Kibune riverside restaurants, Gion kappo, Kodaiji and Nanzenji inns, hotels in Kusatsu, Nagoya and Kyoto, an Asian restaurant in Otsu. Japanese-cuisine cooking-skills certificate 2007; opened Waku in Higashiyama on 14 September 2007, and kept taking stints elsewhere afterwards; fugu licence 2013. Also lists a heavy-motorcycle licence. · Official site: 「京料理を主体としながら、私らしい料理も日々考えております」 — Kyoto cooking at the core, with dishes of his own worked out day by day; 「おもてなしの料理を作りたい」. · Omakase kappo course with counter-side talk.

The fixtures are a small hot pot of carefully drawn dashi, a charcoal-grilled course where you pick the grill, and a kamameshi with the ingredient you choose. Lunch from ¥10,000, dinner from ¥22,000, tax in, no service charge. One diner found the rice pot light on ingredients — the leftovers came back as onigiri to take home.

Closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: Per the official site (junidanya-kyoto.com): 「牛肉の水炊き(しゃぶしゃぶ)発祥の店」. The same owner opened the Hanamikoji shop to make it easier to drop in; the main shop is four doors east, and the site marks the two as separate shops. · Shabu-shabu with house sesame sauce; beef sukiyaki.

Tabelog’s official introduction names the founder Katsuji Nakanishi, who wondered what could be made with one pot, and says the founder’s son now selects the chirimen-jako from Kyushu and Shikoku, paired with Tanba sansho. · Per the official site: "美味しい物は素材が全て" — good food is all in the ingredients. · Ojako-zen; ojako chirimen-sansho.

Went to Italy alone at 18 and cooked mains at the two-star Ristorante Arnolfo in Tuscany, then trained at Villa Fiordaliso on Lake Garda (one star) and Alain Ducasse au Plaza Athénée in Paris (three stars). Back in Japan, head chef of Prinz in Ichijoji, then opening chef for The St. Regis Osaka from 2010; opened erba da nakahigashi in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, in 2016, renamed it 草片 cusavilla on 22 February 2021 with a stronger vegetable focus, and opened ristorante DONO in Okazaki, Kyoto, in April 2024. A May 2026 reviewer names the chef Toshifumi Nakahigashi, second son of the Nakahigashi family; the invoice registration is in the chef’s own name. · Per Tabelog’s official introduction: "Dono" means sharing in Italian — to share nature’s gifts, gathered from the mountains and fields every morning, with guests. · Vegetable and wild-plant courses; matsutake tagliolini in autumn.

places.cu: Korean home cooking: lunch is daeji gukbap — unsalted pork-bone soup with pork belly and shank, seasoned at the table with chive kimchi, gochujang, dried shrimp and miso, with rice or somen and seaweed namul, corn tea free; at night bossam, chijimi (tendon or oyster) from an iron pan, japchae, tteokbokki, bibim noodles, dakhanmari, dak-galbi, kimchi platter, makgeolli (2025–26 reviews)
places.notes: [Korean home cooking · north of Gojo] A small, warm family-run Korean kitchen: at lunch only daeji gukbap, a pork-bone soup you season yourself; at night bossam, crisp chijimi from the iron pan, japchae and makgeolli. About ¥1,500 at lunch, ¥4,000–5,000 at night. One cook, so expect a wait; book dinner; cash only. Closed Thursday.

Featured on TV in 2025 (September 2025 review). · Dwaeji gukbap; bossam; chijimi.

places.notes: [Soba · Gojo Tominokoji, juwari soba on the owner’s own pottery] A bright, renovated room where the owner — soba maker and potter — serves 100% buckwheat soba milled in-house on plates from the studio, with a monthly seasonal bowl and sides of bonito or saba sushi. In the Michelin Guide, and reviewers call it a Bib Gourmand. Expect a queue; order and pay at the door. One July 2026 diner found the noodles clumpy and the soba-yu lukewarm. Lunch only; closed Wednesday and Thursday.

places.notes: [French · Keage, Dominique Bouchet’s dining room in The Westin Miyako] The Westin Miyako’s main French restaurant, supervised by the Paris chef Dominique Bouchet and run by chef 左古 昂: blue lobster jelly with sea urchin and caviar, lobster Parmentier in caviar butter, sauces that are rich but light, a dessert wagon and city views. places.chef: 左古 昂 · Chef since April 2022 (hotel page), Supervised by Dominique Bouchet · Per the hotel page: Dominique Bouchet was chef at La Tour d’Argent and Hôtel de Crillon in Paris, opened Restaurant Dominique Bouchet in Paris’s 8th arrondissement in 2004, and besides Kyoto runs Dominique Bouchet Tokyo in Ginza and the bistro Les Copains de Dominique Bouchet. Chef 左古 昂 trained at Dominique Bouchet Tokyo in Ginza before coming to Kyoto, and has led this kitchen since April 2022. An April 2026 reviewer calls the chef Sako. The same hotel houses Dominique Bouchet Kyoto Le Teppanyaki. · An "evolved classic": carefully chosen Japanese ingredients with traditional French technique, and sauces that are "deep yet light" (hotel page). · Blue lobster jelly with sea urchin and caviar; lobster Parmentier.

The owner pours out the stories of a November 2025 visit by the TV show "Sekkaku Gourmet". Desserts and takeaway sweets by day, a short Italian à la carte by night. Book for weekend lunch. Prices run a little high; busy with tourists.

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Nijo Takakura, open till 2 a.m.] A Showa-feeling okonomiyaki and teppan bar where each dish is finished on the griddle at your table: Kyoto-style beta-yaki and negiyaki, very thin-noodle yakisoba many call the best in town, tonpei-yaki, cheese omelette and cold tofu under spicy chives, with an after-work set of two drinks and two snacks. Run by the chef and a second cook; busy and cramped, so book. Cash only. Lunch and late dinner daily.

places.notes: [Eel · Nishiki Market, upstairs from the river-fish shop] A quiet townhouse-style room above a river-fish shop in busy Nishiki Market, serving its eel since 1912: Kansai-style, grilled over binchotan until the skin crackles, glazed with a sweetish house tare. Bowls from ¥2,100 by the portion (half, two-thirds, whole), hitsumabushi and gozen sets with eel roll and dessert. The kitchen and floor, grill master included, are all women. English menu. Lunch only; closed Wednesday.
